body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text:
[abhyarcana]
śāstrasyāsya praṇetāram abhyarhya sugatātmajaṃ [/]
vaktāraṃ cāsmadādibhyo yatiṣye 'rthavivecane //
body.translated_text: [Salutation] Having honored the author of this treatise, the son of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), and the one who expounded it to us and others, I shall endeavor in the analysis of its meaning.

body.text:
[śāstraśarīra]
tatrāditaḥ śāstraśarīraṃ vyavasthāpyate /
body.translated_text: [Structure of the Treatise] First, the body of the treatise is established.

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ hy āvṛtis tatvaṃ pratipakṣasya bhāvanā /
children.translated_text: Characteristic, obscuration, reality, cultivation of the antidote,

children.text: tatra ca sthā phalaprāptir yānānuttaryam eva ca //
children.translated_text: abiding therein, attainment of the fruit, and the unsurpassability of the vehicle—

body.text: ity ete saptārthā hy asmiṃ cchāstre upadiśyante / yad uta lakṣaṇaṃ āvaraṇaṃ tatvaṃ pratipakṣasya bhāvanā / tasyām eva ca pratipakṣabhāvanāyām avasthā phalaprāptiś ca yānānuttatyañ ca saptamo 'rthaḥ /
body.translated_text: these seven topics are taught in this treatise: namely, characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), obscuration (<s>āvaraṇa</s>), reality (<s>tattva</s>), cultivation of the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvanā</s>), stages in that very cultivation of the antidote, attainment of the fruit, and unsurpassability of the vehicle as the seventh topic.

body.text:
[CHAPTER I. LAKṢAṆAPARICCHEDA]
[1. abhūtaparikalpa; a. sadasallaksaṇa]
tatra lakṣaṇam ārabhyāha /
body.translated_text: [CHAPTER I: Section on Characteristics] Therein, beginning with 'characteristic,' he says:

children.text:
abhūtaparikalpo 'sti dvayan tatra na vidyate /
śūnyatā vidyate tv atra tasyām api sa vidyate // 1.1
children.translated_text: Unreal imagination (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>) exists; duality is not found therein. Emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), however, is found therein; and in that [emptiness], it [unreal imagination] too is found. [1.1]

body.text: tatrābhūtaparikalpo grāhyagrāhakavikalpaḥ / dvayaṃ grāhyaṃ grāhakañ ca / śūnyatā tasyābhūtaparikalpasya grāhyagrāhakabhāvena virahitatā / tasyām api sa vidyata ity abhūtaparikalpaḥ / evaṃ yad yatra nāsti tat tena śūnyam iti yathābhūtaṃ samanupaśyati yat punar atrāvaśiṣṭaṃ bhavati tat sad ihāstīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīty aviparītaṃ śūnyatālakṣaṇam udbhāvitaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Therein, 'unreal imagination' is the discrimination of grasped and grasper (<s>grāhya-grāhaka-vikalpa</s>). 'Duality' is the grasped and the grasper. 'Emptiness' is the separation of that unreal imagination from the nature of grasped and grasper. 'In that [emptiness] too it is found' means unreal imagination [is found in emptiness]. Thus, 'what does not exist in something, that is correctly seen as empty of that'; and 'what remains here, that is correctly known as existing here'—thus the undistorted definition of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is brought forth.

children.text:
na śūnyaṃ nāpi cāśūnyaṃ tasmāt sarvaṃ vidhīyate /
satvād asatvāt satvāc ca madhyamā pratipac ca sā // I.2
children.translated_text: Neither empty nor non-empty—therefore everything is declared. Because of the existence [of unreal imagination], because of the non-existence [of duality], and because of the existence [of emptiness], that is the middle path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>). [1.2]

body.text: na śūnyaṃ śūnyatayā cābhūtaparikalpena ca / na cāśūnyaṃ dvayena grāhyena grāhakeṇa ca / sarvaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ cābhūtaparikalpākhyaṃ / asaṃskṛtaṃ ca śūnyatākhyaṃ / vidhīyate nirdiśyate satvād abhūtaparikalpasya asatvād dvayasya satvāc ca śūnyatāyā abhūtaparikalpe tasyāṃ cābhūtaparikalpasya sā ca madhyamā pratipat / yat sarvaṃ / naikāntena śūnyaṃ naikāntenāśūnyaṃ / evam ayaṃ pāṭhaḥ prajñāpāramitādiṣv anulomito bhavati sarvam idaṃ na śūnyaṃ nāpi cāśūnyam iti /
body.translated_text: Not empty—because of emptiness and because of unreal imagination. Not non-empty—because of the duality of grasped and grasper. 'Everything'—both the conditioned, called unreal imagination, and the unconditioned, called emptiness—is 'declared,' is taught. Because of the existence of unreal imagination, because of the non-existence of duality, and because of the existence of emptiness in unreal imagination and of unreal imagination in it—that is the middle path. For everything is neither exclusively empty nor exclusively non-empty. Thus this reading follows the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and other [sūtras].

body.text:
[b. Svalakṣaṇa]
evam abhūtaparikalpasya sallakṣaṇam asallakṣaṇaṃ ca khyāpayitvā / svalakṣaṇaṃ khyāpayati /
body.translated_text: [b. Own-characteristic] Having thus made known the existent and non-existent characteristics of unreal imagination, he makes known its own-characteristic:

children.text:
arthasatvātmavijñaptipratibhāsaṃ prajāyate /
vijñānaṃ nāsti cāsyārthas tadabhāvāt tad apy asat // I.3
children.translated_text: Consciousness arises with the appearance of object, being, self, and representation. Its object does not exist; because of that absence, it too is unreal. [1.3]

body.text: tatrārthapratibhāsaṃ yad rūpādibhāvena pratibhāsate / satvapratibhāsaṃ yat pañcendriyatvena svaparasantānayor [/] ātmapratibhāsaṃ kliṣṭaṃ manaḥ / ātmamohādisaṃprayogāt / vijñaptipratibhāsaṃ ṣaḍ vijñānāni [/] nāsti cāsyārtha iti / arthasatvapratibhāsasyānākāratvāt / ātmavijñaptipratibhāsasya ca vitathapratibhāsatvāt / (

children.translated_text: [<s>Mvbh</s> 19]

children.text: ) tadabhāvāt tad apy asad iti / yat tadgrāhyaṃ rūpādipañcendriyaṃ manaḥ ṣaḍvijñānasaṃjñakaṃ caturvidhaṃ tasya grāhyasyārthasyābhāvāt tad api grāhakaṃ vijñānam asat /
children.translated_text: 'Because of that absence, it too is unreal'—that fourfold [entity]—the grasped, designated as visible matter etc., the five sense-faculties, the mind, and the six consciousnesses—because of the non-existence of that grasped object, the grasping consciousness too is unreal.

body.translated_text: Therein, 'appearing as object'—what appears in the form of visible matter etc. 'Appearing as being'—what [appears] as the five sense-faculties in one's own and others' continua. 'Appearing as self'—the afflicted mind (<s>kliṣṭa manas</s>), because of its association with self-delusion etc. 'Appearing as representation'—the six consciousnesses. 'Its object does not exist'—because the appearance of object and being is without [corresponding] form; and because the appearance of self and representation is a false appearance.

children.text:
abhūtaparikalpatvaṃ siddham asya bhavaty ataḥ /
na tathā sarvathābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore the nature of unreal imagination is established for this [consciousness]. Not so [would it be] if there were complete non-existence.

body.text: yasmān na tathāsya bhāvo yathā pratibhāsa utpadyate / na ca sarvathābhāvo bhrāntimātrasyotpādāt/ kimarthaṃ punas tasyābhāva eva neṣyate / yasmāt /
body.translated_text: Because its mode of being is not as [it] appears when arising. Yet it is not completely non-existent, because of the arising of mere illusion. For what reason is its non-existence alone not accepted? Because:

children.translated_text: From the destruction of that, liberation is accepted. [1.4]

body.text: anyathā na bandho na mokṣaḥ prasidhyed iti saṃkleśavyavadānāpavādadoṣaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: Otherwise, neither bondage nor liberation would be established—the fault of denying defilement and purification would arise.

body.text:
[c. Saṃgrahalakṣaṇa]
evam abhūtaparikalpasya svalakṣaṇaṃ khyāpayitvā saṃgrahalakṣaṇaṃ khyāpayati / abhūtaparikalpamātre sati yathā trayāṇāṃ svabhāvānāṃ saṃgraho bhavati /
body.translated_text: [c. Inclusion-characteristic] Having thus made known the own-characteristic of unreal imagination, he makes known the inclusion-characteristic—how, given merely unreal imagination, there is an inclusion of the three natures (<s>svabhāvas</s>):

children.text:
kalpitaḥ paratantraś ca pariniṣpanna eva ca /
arthād abhūtakalpāc ca dvayābhāvāc ca deśitaḥ // I.5
children.translated_text: The imagined (<s>kalpita</s>), the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), and the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) are taught from the [grasped] object, from unreal imagination, and from the absence of duality respectively. [1.5]

body.text: arthaḥ parikalpitaḥ svabhāvaḥ / abhūtaparikalpaḥ paratantraḥ svabhāvaḥ / grāhyagrāhakābhāvaḥ pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: The object is the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s>). Unreal imagination is the dependent nature (<s>paratantra-svabhāva</s>). The absence of grasped and grasper is the perfected nature (<s>pariniṣpanna-svabhāva</s>).

body.text:
[d. Asallakṣaṇānupraveśopāyalakṣaṇa]
idānīṃ tasminn evābhūtaparikalpe 'sallakṣaṇānupraveśopāyalakṣaṇaṃ paridīpayati /
body.translated_text: [d. Characteristic of the Means of Entering the Non-existent Characteristic] Now, regarding that very unreal imagination, he illuminates the characteristic of the means of entering the non-existent characteristic:

children.text:
upalabdhiṃ samāśritya nopalabdhiḥ prajāyate /
nopalabdhiṃ samāśritya nopalabdhiḥ prajāyate // I.6
children.translated_text: Relying on apprehension, non-apprehension arises. Relying on non-apprehension, non-apprehension [of apprehension] arises. [1.6]

body.text: vijñaptimātropalabdhiṃ niśrityārthānupalabdhir jāyate / arthānupalabdhiṃ niśritya vijñaptimātrasyāpy anupalabdhir jāyate / evam asallakṣaṇaṃ grāhyagrāhakayoḥ praviśati /
body.translated_text: Relying on the apprehension of mere representation (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>), the non-apprehension of the object arises. Relying on the non-apprehension of the object, the non-apprehension even of mere representation arises. Thus the non-existent characteristic of grasped and grasper is entered.

body.text: upalabdhes tataḥ siddhā nopalabdhisvabhāvatā /
body.translated_text: Therefore, from apprehension, the nature of non-apprehension is established.

body.text: upalabhyārthābhāve upalabdhyayogāt /
body.translated_text: Because, when the object is found to be absent, apprehension is impossible.

children.text: tasmāc ca samatā jñeyā nopalambhopalambhayoḥ // I.7
children.translated_text: Therefore the equality of non-apprehension and apprehension should be known. [1.7]

body.text: upalabdher upalabdhitvenāsiddhatvād abhūtārthapratibhāsatayā tūpalabdhir ity ucyate 'nupalabdhisvabhāvāpi satī
body.translated_text: Because apprehension is not established as [truly] apprehending—but is called 'apprehension' only because of the appearance of an unreal object—even while being of the nature of non-apprehension.

body.text:
[e. Prabhedalakṣaṇa]
tasyaivedānīm abhūtaparikalpasya prabhedalakṣaṇaṃ khyāpayati /
body.translated_text: [e. Classification-characteristic] Now he makes known the classification-characteristic of that very unreal imagination:

body.text: abhūtaparikalpaś ca cittacaittās tridhātukāḥ /
body.translated_text: Unreal imagination is mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caittas</s>) of the three realms.

body.text: kāmarūpārūpyāvacarabhedena /
body.translated_text: Differentiated as the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm.

body.text:
[f. Paryāyalakṣaṇa]
paryāyalakṣaṇaṃ ca khyāpayati /
body.translated_text: [f. Synonym-characteristic] He also makes known the synonym-characteristic:

children.text: tatrārthadṛṣṭir vijñānaṃ tadviśeṣe tu caitasāḥ // I.8
children.translated_text: Therein, the seeing of the object is consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>); but regarding its specifications, [the seeing is by] the mental factors. [1.8]

body.text: tatrārthamātre dṛṣṭir vijñānaṃ / arthaviśeṣe dṛṣṭiś caitasā vedanādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the seeing of the mere object is consciousness. The seeing of the specification of the object is the mental factors—feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) and the rest.

body.text:
[g. Pravṛttilakṣaṇa]
pravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ ca khyāpayati /
body.translated_text: [g. Activity-characteristic] He also makes known the activity-characteristic:

children.text:
ekaṃ pratyayavijñānaṃ dvitīyam aupabhogikaṃ /
upabhogaparicchedaprerakās tatra caitasāḥ // I.9
children.translated_text: One [consciousness] is the causal consciousness; the second is the experiential [consciousness]. The mental factors therein are the determiners, discriminators, and impellers of experience. [1.9]

body.text: ālayavijñānam anyeṣāṃ vijñānānāṃ pratyayatvāt pratyayavijñānaṃ / tatpratyayaṃ pravṛttivijñānam aupabhogikaṃ / upabhogo vedanā / paricchedaḥ saṃjñā / prerakāḥ saṃskārā vijñānasya cetanāmanaskārādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: The storehouse consciousness (<s>ālaya-vijñāna</s>), being the condition of other consciousnesses, is the 'causal consciousness.' The active consciousness (<s>pravṛtti-vijñāna</s>), conditioned by that, is the 'experiential.' Experience (<s>upabhoga</s>) is feeling (<s>vedanā</s>). Discrimination (<s>pariccheda</s>) is perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>). The impellers (<s>prerakāḥ</s>) are the formations (<s>saṃskārās</s>)—volition (<s>cetanā</s>), attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), and the rest—of consciousness.

body.text:
[h. Saṃkleśalaksaṇa]
saṃkleśalakṣaṇaṃ ca khyāpayati/
body.translated_text: [h. Defilement-characteristic] He also makes known the defilement-characteristic:

children.text:
chādanād ropaṇāc caiva nayanāt saṃparigrahāt /
pūraṇāt triparicchedād upabhogāc ca karṣaṇāt // I.10
children.translated_text: Through covering, through implanting, through leading, through appropriating, through filling, through triple discrimination, through experiencing, and through dragging, [1.10]

body.text: nibandhanād ābhimukhyād duḥkhanāt kliśyate jagat /
body.translated_text: through binding, through facing [rebirth], and through causing suffering, the world is afflicted.

body.text: tatra cchādanād avidyayā yathābhūtadarśanavibandhanāt / ropaṇāt saṃskārair vijñāne karmavāsanāyāḥ pratiṣṭhāpanāt / nayanād vijñānenopapattisthānasaṃprāpaṇāt / saṃparigrahān nāmarūpeṇātmabhāvasya / pūraṇāt ṣaḍāyatanena / triparicchedāt sparśena / upabhogād vedanayā / karṣaṇāt tṛṣṇayā karmākṣiptasya punarbhavasya [/] nibandhanād upādānair vijñānasyotpattyanukūleṣu kāmādiṣu / ābhimukhyād bhavena kṛtasya karmaṇaḥ punarbhave vipākadānāyābhimukhīkaraṇāt / duḥkhanāj jātyā jarāmaraṇena ca parikliśyate jagat / so 'yaṃ /
body.translated_text: Therein: through 'covering' by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>)—the obstruction of seeing things as they are; through 'implanting' by formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>)—the establishment of <s>karma</s>-impressions in consciousness; through 'leading' by consciousness—bringing [beings] to the place of rebirth; through 'appropriating' by name-and-form—[the appropriation of] the self-existence; through 'filling' by the six sense-bases; through 'triple discrimination' by contact; through 'experiencing' by feeling; through 'dragging' by craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>)—of the re-existence projected by <s>karma</s>; through 'binding' by grasping (<s>upādāna</s>)—of consciousness in the favorable conditions of desire etc.; through 'facing' by becoming (<s>bhava</s>)—

children.text: tredhā dvedhā ca saṃkleśaḥ saptadhābhūtakalpanāt // I.11
children.translated_text: Defilement is threefold, twofold, and sevenfold, from unreal imagination. [1.11]

body.text: tredhā saṃkleśaḥ / kleśasaṃkleśaḥ karmasaṃkleśaḥ janmasaṃkleśaś ca / tatra kleśasaṃkleśo 'vidyātṛṣṇopādānāni / karmasaṃkleśaḥ saṃskārā bhavaś ca / janmasaṃkleśaḥ śeṣāṇy aṅgāni / dvedhā saṃkleśaḥ / hetusaṃkleśaḥ phalasaṃkleśaś ca / (

children.translated_text: [<s>Mvbh</s> 22]

children.text: ) tatra hetusaṃkleśaḥ kleśakarmasvabhāvair aṅgaiḥ phalasaṃkleśaś ca śeṣaiḥ / saptadhā saṃkleśaḥ saptavidho hetuḥ / viparyāsahetuḥ / ākṣepahetuḥ i upanayahetuḥ / parigrahahetuḥ / upabhogahetuḥ / ākarṣaṇahetuḥ / udvegahetuś ca / tatra viparyāsahetur avidyā / ākṣepahetuḥ saṃskārāḥ / upanayahetur vijñānaṃ / parigrahahetur nāmarūpaṣaḍāyatane / upabhogahetuḥ sparśavedane / ākarṣaṇahetus tṛṣṇopādānabhavāḥ / udvegahetur jātijarāmaraṇe / sarvaś caiṣa saṃkleśo 'bhūtaparikalpāt pravartata iti /
children.translated_text: Therein, causal defilement is through links of the nature of afflictions and actions; resultant defilement is through the remaining [links]. Defilement is sevenfold, [meaning] a sevenfold cause: the cause of distortion (<s>viparyāsa</s>); the cause of projection (<s>ākṣepa</s>); the cause of leading (<s>upanaya</s>); the cause of appropriation (<s>parigraha</s>); the cause of experience (<s>upabhoga</s>); the cause of dragging (<s>ākarṣaṇa</s>); and the cause of agitation (<s>udvega</s>). Therein: the cause of distortion is ignorance; the cause of projection is formations; the cause of leading is consciousness; the cause of appropriation is name-and-form and the six sense-bases; the cause of experience is contact and feeling; the cause of dragging is craving, grasping, and becoming.

body.translated_text: Defilement is threefold: defilement of afflictions (<s>kleśa-saṃkleśa</s>), defilement of action (<s>karma-saṃkleśa</s>), and defilement of birth (<s>janma-saṃkleśa</s>). Therein, the defilement of afflictions consists of ignorance, craving, and grasping. The defilement of action consists of formations and becoming. The defilement of birth consists of the remaining [dependent origination] links. Defilement is twofold: causal defilement and resultant defilement.

body.text:
[Abhūtaparikalpapiṇḍārtha]
piṇḍārthaḥ punar abhūtaparikalpasya navavidhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitaṃ bhavati / sallakṣaṇaṃ / asallakṣaṇaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ / saṃgrahalakṣaṇaṃ [/] asallakṣaṇānupraveśopāyalakṣaṇaṃ / prabhedalakṣaṇaṃ / paryāyalakṣaṇaṃ / pravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ / saṃkleśalakṣaṇañ ca /
body.translated_text: [Summary meaning of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (false imagination)] Furthermore, the summary meaning of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (false imagination) is illuminated through nine characteristics: the characteristic of existence, the characteristic of non-existence, the intrinsic characteristic, the characteristic of inclusion, the characteristic of the means of entering into the characteristic of non-existence, the characteristic of division, the characteristic of synonyms, the characteristic of functioning, and the characteristic of defilement.

body.text:
[2. Śūnyatā]
evam abhūtaparikalpaṃ khyāpayitvā yathā śūnyatā vijñeyā tan nirdiśati /
body.translated_text: [2. <s>Śūnyatā</s> (Emptiness)] Having thus made known <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (false imagination), he indicates how <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is to be understood.

children.text:
lakṣaṇaṃ cātha paryāyas tadartho bheda eva ca /
sādhanaṃ ceti vijñeyaṃ śūnyatāyāḥ samāsataḥ // I.12
children.translated_text: The characteristic, then the synonyms, their meaning, division indeed, and the establishment — these are to be understood regarding <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), in brief. // I.12

body.text:
[a. Sūnyatālakṣaṇa]
kathaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vijñeyaṃ /
body.translated_text: [a. Characteristic of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)] How is the characteristic to be understood?

body.text: dvayābhāvo hy abhāvasya bhāvaḥ śūnyasya lakṣaṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: The absence of duality and the existence of that absence is the characteristic of the empty.

body.text: dvayagrāhyagrāhakasyābhāvaḥ / tasya cābhāvasya bhāvaḥ śūnyatayā (

children.translated_text: Mvbh 23

children.text: ) lakṣaṇam ity abhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇatvaṃ śūnyatāyāḥ paridīpitaṃ bhavati / yaś cāsau tadabhāvasvabhāvaḥ sa /
children.translated_text: is the characteristic — thus the characteristic of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) as having the nature of absence is illuminated. And that which is the nature of the absence of that [duality],

body.translated_text: The duality is the absence of the apprehended and the apprehender. And the existence of that absence, by means of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),

body.text: na bhāvo nāpi cābhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: is neither existence nor non-existence.

body.text: kathaṃ na bhāvo yasmāt dvayasyābhāvaḥ / kathaṃ nābhāvo yasmāt dvayābhāvasya bhāvaḥ / etac ca śūnyatāyā lakṣaṇaṃ / tasmād abhūtaparikalpān
body.translated_text: How is it not existence? Because it is the absence of duality. How is it not non-existence? Because there is the existence of the absence of duality. And this is the characteristic of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). Therefore, from <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (false imagination),

children.translated_text: it has neither a separate nor an identical characteristic. // I.13

body.text: pṛthaktve sati dharmād anyā dharmateti na yujyate / anityatāduḥkhatāvat / ekatve sati viśuddhyālambanaṃ jñānaṃ na syāt sāmānyalakṣaṇañ ca / etena tattvānyatvavinirmuktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: If they were separate, then <s>dharmatā</s> (the true nature of things) being other than <s>dharma</s> (phenomena) would not be tenable — just as with impermanence and suffering. If they were identical, then knowledge having purification as its object would not exist, nor would the general characteristic. By this, the characteristic as free from both identity and difference is illuminated.

body.text:
[b. Sūnyatāparyāya]
kathaṃ paryāyo vijñeyaḥ /
body.translated_text: [b. Synonyms of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)] How are the synonyms to be understood?

children.text:
tathatā bhūtakoṭiś cānimittaṃ paramārthatā /
dharmadhātuś ca paryāyāḥ śūnyatāyāḥ samāsataḥ // I.14
children.translated_text: <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the ultimate point of reality), <s>animitta</s> (the signless), <s>paramārthatā</s> (ultimate truth), and <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of phenomena) — these are the synonyms of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), in brief. // I.14

body.text:
[c. Śūnyatāparyāyārtha]
kathaṃ paryāyārtho vijñeyaḥ /
body.translated_text: [c. Meaning of the synonyms of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)] How is the meaning of the synonyms to be understood?

children.text:
ananyathāviparyāsatannirodhāryagocaraiḥ /
hetutvāc cāryadharmāṇāṃ paryāyārtho yathākramaṃ // I.15
children.translated_text: By not being otherwise, by non-inversion, by the cessation of that, by being the domain of the noble ones, and because of being the cause of the noble qualities — the meaning of the synonyms is in due order. // I.15

body.text: ananyathārthena tathātā nityan tathaiveti kṛtvā [/] aviparyāsārthena bhūtakoṭiḥ viparyāsāvastutvāt / nimittanirodhārthenānimittaṃ sarvanimittābhāvāt / āryajñānagocaratvāt paramārthaḥ / paramajñānaviṣayatvād [/] āryadharmahetutvād dharmadhātuḥ / (

children.translated_text: Mvbh 24

children.text: ) āryadharmāṇān tadālambanaprabhavatvāt / hetvartho hy atra dhātvarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: because the noble qualities arise with that as their support. For here the meaning of <s>dhātu</s> is the meaning of cause.

body.translated_text: In the sense of not being otherwise, it is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), since it is always just so. In the sense of non-inversion, it is <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the ultimate point of reality), because inversions are unreal. In the sense of the cessation of signs, it is <s>animitta</s> (the signless), because of the absence of all signs. Because of being the domain of noble knowledge, it is <s>paramārtha</s> (the ultimate truth), because of being the object of the highest knowledge. Because of being the cause of noble qualities, it is <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of phenomena),

body.text:
[d. Śūnyatāprabheda]
kathaṃ śūnyatāyāḥ prabhedo jñeyaḥ /
body.translated_text: [d. Division of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)] How is the division of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) to be known?

body.text: saṃkliṣṭā ca viśuddhā ca /
body.translated_text: Defiled and purified —

body.text: ity asyāḥ prabhedaḥ / kasyām avasthāyāṃ saṃkliṣṭā kasyāṃ viśuddhā /
body.translated_text: such is its division. In which state is it defiled, and in which purified?

body.text: samalā nirmalā ca sā /
body.translated_text: It is with defilement and without defilement.

body.text: yadā saha malena vartate tadā saṃkliṣṭā / yadā prahīṇamalā tadā viśuddhā / yadi samalā bhūtvā nirmalā bhavati kathaṃ vikāradharmiṇītvād anityā na bhavati / yasmād asyāḥ
body.translated_text: When it exists together with defilement, then it is defiled. When the defilement has been abandoned, then it is purified. If it becomes without defilement after having been with defilement, how does it not become impermanent, since it would be subject to change? Because its

children.translated_text: purification is held to be like the purification of the water element, gold, and space. // I.16

body.text: āgantukamalāpagamān na tu tasyāḥ svabhāvānyatvaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Through the removal of adventitious defilements, there is no alteration of its own nature.

body.text: [Ṣoḍaśavidhā śūnyatā]
body.translated_text: [The sixteen types of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)]

body.text: ayam aparaḥ prabhedaḥ ṣoḍaśavidhā śūnyatā / adhyātmaśūnyatā / bahirdhāśūnyatā / adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā / mahāśūnyatā / śūnyatāśūnyatā / paramārthaśūnyatā / saṃskṛtaśūnyatā / asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā / atyantaśūnyatā / anavarāgrasūnyatā / anavakāraśūnyatā / prakṛtiśūnyatā / lakṣaṇaśūnyatā / sarvadharmaśūnyatā / abhāvaśūnyatā / abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā ca / saiṣā samāsato veditavyā /
body.translated_text: Here is another division — the sixteen types of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness): <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal), <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the external), <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal and external), <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (great emptiness), <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness), <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the ultimate), <s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the conditioned), <s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the unconditioned), <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s> (absolute emptiness), <s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of what is without beginning or end), <s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-abandonment), <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of inherent nature), <s>lakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of characteristics), <s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of all phenomena), <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-existence), and <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the own-nature of non-existence). This is to be understood in brief.

children.text:
bhoktṛbhojanataddehapratiṣṭhāvastuśūnyatā /
(Mvbh 25)
tac ca yena yathā dṛṣṭaṃ yadarthaṃtasya śūnyatā // I.171
children.translated_text: Emptiness of the enjoyer, the enjoyed, their body, and the basis of existence; and that by which and in the manner in which it is seen, and for what purpose — the emptiness of that. // I.17

body.text: tatra bhoktṛśūnyatā (/) ādhyātmikāny āyatanāny ārabdhā bhojanaśūnyatā bāhyāni / taddehas tayor bhoktṛbhojanayor yad adhiṣṭhānaṃ śarīraṃ [/] tasya śūnyatādhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatety ucyate / pratiṣṭhāvastu bhājanalokaḥ [/] tasya vistīrṇatvāc chūnyatā mahāśūnyatety ucyate / tac cādhyātmikāyatanādi yena śūnyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śūnyatājñānena [/] tasya śūnyatā śūnyatāśūnyatā / yathā ca dṛṣṭaṃ paramārthākāreṇa tasya śūnyatā paramārtha śūnyatā / yadarthaṃ ca bodhisatvaḥ prapadyate tasya ca śūnyatā / kimarthañ ca prapadyate /
body.translated_text: There, the emptiness of the enjoyer — this is in reference to the internal <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases). The emptiness of the enjoyed is the external ones. Their body is the support of the enjoyer and the enjoyed, namely the physical body; its emptiness is called <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal and external). The basis of existence is the vessel-world; its emptiness, on account of its vastness, is called <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (great emptiness). And that by which the internal sense bases and so forth are seen as empty, namely by the knowledge of emptiness — its emptiness is <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness). And the manner in which it is seen, namely under the aspect of ultimate reality — its emptiness is <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the ultimate). And for what purpose does the <s>bodhisattva</s> engage? Its emptiness too. For what purpose does he engage?

body.text: śubhadvayasya prāptyarthaṃ /
body.translated_text: For the purpose of attaining the two goods —

body.text: kuśalasya saṃskṛtasyāsaṃskṛtasya ca /
body.translated_text: the wholesome that is conditioned and the unconditioned.

body.text: sadā satvahitāya ca /
body.translated_text: And for the perpetual benefit of beings —

body.text: atyantasatvahitārthaṃ /
body.translated_text: for the purpose of the absolute benefit of beings.

body.text: saṃsārātyajanārthañ ca /
body.translated_text: And for the purpose of not abandoning <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) —

body.text: anavarāgrasya hi saṃsārasya śūnyatām apaśyan khinnaḥ saṃsāraṃ parityajeta /
body.translated_text: For if one who does not see the emptiness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) which is without beginning or end becomes weary, one would abandon <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.translated_text: And for the imperishability of the wholesome. // I.18

body.text: nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇe 'pi yan nāvakirati notsṛjati tasya śūnyatā (/) (

children.translated_text: Mvbh 26
is called <s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-abandonment).

body.translated_text: Even in <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder, that which one does not scatter or abandon — its emptiness

body.text: gotrasya ca viśuddhyarthaṃ /
body.translated_text: And for the purpose of the purification of the spiritual lineage —

body.text: gotraṃ hi prakṛtiḥ svābhāvikatvāt /
body.translated_text: For <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage) is <s>prakṛti</s> (inherent nature), because of its being innate.

body.text: lakṣaṇavyañjanāptaye /
body.translated_text: For the attainment of the marks and minor marks —

body.text: mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇānāṃ sānuvyañjanānāṃ prāptaye /
body.translated_text: for the attainment of the marks of a <s>mahāpuruṣa</s> (great being) together with the minor marks.

children.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> engages for the purification of the <s>buddhadharmas</s> (qualities of a Buddha). // I.19

body.text: balavaiśāradyāveṇikādīnāṃ / evan tāvac caturdaśānāṃ śūnyatānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyaṃ / kā punar atra śūnyatā /
body.translated_text: Such as the powers, the fearlessnesses, the distinctive qualities, and so forth. Thus, the establishment of fourteen types of emptiness is to be understood. But what here is emptiness?

children.text:
pudgalasyātha dharmāṇām abhāvaḥ śūnyatātra hi /
tadabhāvasya sadbhāvas tasmin sā śūnyatāparā // I.20
children.translated_text: The absence of a person and of phenomena is emptiness here; and the real existence of that absence — in that, the other emptiness. // I.20

body.text: pudgaladharmābhāvaś ca śūnyatā / tadabhāvasya ca sadbhāvaḥ [/] tasmin yathokte bhoktrādau sānyā śūnyateti [/] śūnyatālakṣaṇakhyāpanārthaṃ dvividhām ante śūnyatāṃ vyavasthāpayati / abhāvaśūnyatām abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāṃ ca / pudgaladharmasamāropasya tacchūnyatāpavādasya ca parihārārthaṃ yathākramaṃ / evaṃ śūnyatāyāḥ prabhedo vijñeyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The absence of <s>pudgala</s> (person) and <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) is emptiness. And the real existence of that absence, in that which has been described — the enjoyer and so forth — is the other emptiness. For the purpose of making known the characteristic of emptiness, he establishes a twofold emptiness at the end: <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-existence) and <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the own-nature of non-existence) — in due order, for the purpose of countering the superimposition of a person and phenomena, and the denial of the emptiness of that. Thus, the division of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is to be understood.

body.text:
[e. Śūnyatāsādhana]
kathaṃ sādhanaṃ vijñeyaṃ /
body.translated_text: [e. Establishment of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)] How is the establishment to be understood?

children.text:
saṃkliṣṭā ced bhaven nāsau muktāḥ syuḥ sarvadehinaḥ /
viśuddhā ced bhaven nāsau vyāyāmo niṣphalo bhavet // I.21
children.translated_text: If it were defiled, there would be no liberation — all embodied beings would be liberated. If it were purified, then effort would be fruitless. // I.21

body.text: yadi dharmāṇāṃ śūnyatā āgantukair upakleśair anutpanne (

children.translated_text: Mvbh 27

children.text: ) 'pi pratipakṣe na saṃkliṣṭā bhavet saṃkleśābhāvād ayatnata eva muktāḥ sarvasatvā bhaveyuḥ / athotpanne 'pi pratipakṣe na viśuddhā bhavet mokṣārtham ārambho niṣphalo bhavet / evaṃ ca kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: then, because of the absence of defilement, all beings would be liberated effortlessly. Or if, even when the antidote has arisen, it were not purified, then the endeavor for liberation would be fruitless. This being so,

body.translated_text: If the <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of phenomena, through adventitious defilements, were not defiled even when the antidote has not arisen,

body.text: na kliṣṭā nāpi vākliṣṭā śuddhāśuddhā na caiva sā /
body.translated_text: It is neither defiled nor undefiled, neither pure nor impure.

body.text: kathaṃ na kliṣṭā nāpi cāśuddhā / prakṛtyaiva /
body.translated_text: How is it not defiled and yet not pure? By its very nature —

body.text: prahhāsvaratvāc cittasya /
body.translated_text: because the mind is luminous by nature.

body.text: kathaṃ nākliṣṭā na śuddhā /
body.translated_text: How is it not undefiled and not pure?

children.translated_text: Because the defilements are adventitious. // I.22

body.text: evaṃ śūnyatāyā uddiṣṭaḥ prabhedaḥ sādhito bhavati /
body.translated_text: Thus, the division of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) that was stated is established.

body.text:
[Śūnyatāpiṇḍārtha]
tatra śūnyatāyāḥ piṇḍārthaḥ / lakṣaṇato vyavasthānataś ca veditavyaḥ / tatra lakṣaṇato 'bhāvalakṣaṇato bhāvalakṣaṇataś ca / bhāvalakṣaṇaṃ punar bhāvābhāvavinirmuktalakṣaṇataś ca / tatvānyatvavinirmuktalakṣaṇataś ca / vyavasthānaṃ punaḥ paryāyādivyavasthānato veditavyaṃ / tatraitayā catuḥprakāradeśanayā śūnyatāyāḥ svalakṣaṇaṃ / karmalakṣaṇaṃ / saṃkleśavyavadānalakṣaṇaṃ / yuktilakṣaṇaṃ codbhāvitaṃ bhavati / vikalpatrāsakauśīdyavicikitsopaśāntaye /
body.translated_text: [Summary meaning of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)] Therein, the summary meaning of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is to be understood in terms of its characteristic and its establishment. As to the characteristic, it is in terms of the characteristic of absence and the characteristic of existence. The characteristic of existence, moreover, is in terms of a characteristic free from both existence and non-existence, and a characteristic free from both identity and difference. The establishment, moreover, is to be understood in terms of the establishment of synonyms and so forth. Therein, by means of this fourfold teaching, the intrinsic characteristic, the functional characteristic, the characteristic of defilement and purification, and the characteristic of reasoning of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) are brought to light. For the pacification of discriminating fear, sloth, and doubt,

body.text: madhyāntavibhāge /akṣaṇaparicchedaḥ prathamaḥ // //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Madhyāntavibhāga</s>, the first chapter on characteristics is concluded. //

body.text:
[CHAPTER II. ĀVARAṆAPARICCHEDA]
[1. Vyāpyādipañcāvaraṇa]
body.translated_text: [CHAPTER II. CHAPTER ON OBSCURATIONS] [1. The five obscurations: pervasive and so forth]

body.text: āvaraṇam adhikṛtyāha /
body.translated_text: With reference to obscurations, he says:

children.translated_text: The pervasive, the partial, the excessive, the equal, and the abandonment — the twofold obscuration is declared.

body.text: tatra vyāpi kleśajñeyāvaraṇaṃ bodhisatvagotrakāṇāṃ kaṃ sākalyāt / prādeśikaṃ kleśāvaranaṃ śrāvakādigotrakāṇāṃ / udriktaṃ teṣām eva rāgādicaritānāṃ / samaṃ samabhāgacaritānāṃ / saṃsārādānatyāgāvaraṇaṃ bodhisatvagotrakāṇām apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇāvaraṇād ity etad yathāyogam ubhayeṣām āvaraṇam ākhyātaṃ / bodhisatvagotrakānāṃ śrāvakādigotrakāṇāṃ ca /
body.translated_text: There, the pervasive is the obscuration of <s>kleśa</s> (afflictions) and <s>jñeya</s> (the knowable), belonging to those of the <s>bodhisattva</s> lineage, because of its totality. The partial is the <s>kleśāvaraṇa</s> (obscuration of afflictions) belonging to those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) lineage and others. The excessive belongs to those same ones who are of the temperament dominated by passion and the rest. The equal belongs to those of balanced temperament. The obscuration of not abandoning the taking up of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) belongs to those of the <s>bodhisattva</s> lineage, because of the obscuration to non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> — thus this twofold obscuration is declared as applying respectively to both: those of the <s>bodhisattva</s> lineage and those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> lineage and others.

body.text: [2. Prayoganavasaṃyojanāvaraṇa]
body.translated_text: [2. Obscurations of the nine fetters in practice]

body.text: punar
body.translated_text: Furthermore,

children.translated_text: the characteristic of <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) is ninefold. // II.1

body.text: saṃyojanāny āvaraṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: The fetters (<s>saṃyojanas</s>) are the obstruction.

body.text: nava saṃyojanāni (/) kleśāvaraṇaṃ / kasyaitasyāvaraṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: The nine fetters constitute the obstruction of the afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>). What is this an obstruction of?

children.translated_text: Of spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>) and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), and of seeing the truth (<s>tattvadarśana</s>).

body.text: anunayasaṃyojanaṃ saṃvegasyāvaraṇaṃ [/] pratighasaṃyojanam (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 29]

children.text: ) upekṣīyāḥ / tena hi pratikūlam api pratighavastu upekṣituṃ na śaknoti / śeṣāni tattvadarśanasyāvaraṇaṃ / kathaṃ kṛtvā / tāni hi yathākramaṃ /
children.translated_text: to equanimity. For due to [aversion], one cannot maintain equanimity even toward disagreeable objects of aversion. The remaining [fetters] are obstructions to seeing the truth. How so? They are, in their respective order:

body.translated_text: The fetter of attraction (<s>anunaya</s>) is an obstruction to spiritual urgency. The fetter of aversion (<s>pratigha</s>) [is an obstruction]

children.translated_text: Of the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and of its object as well — (II.2)

children.text:
nirodhamārgaratneṣu lābhasatkāra eva ca /
saṃlekhasya parijñāne /
children.translated_text: Regarding cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), the path (<s>mārga</s>), the [Three] Jewels (<s>ratna</s>), gain (<s>lābha</s>), and honor (<s>satkāra</s>); and of self-mortification (<s>saṃlekha</s>) and full understanding (<s>parijñāna</s>) —

body.text: saṃyojanāny āvaraṇaṃ bhavaṃti / mānasaṃyojanaṃ hi satkāyadṛṣṭiparijñāne bhavaty āvaraṇaṃ / abhisamayakāle sāntaravyantarāsmimānasamudācāravaśena tadaprahāṇāt / avidyāsaṃyojanaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭivastuparijñāne / tenopādānaskandhāparijñānāt / dṛṣṭisaṃyojanaṃ nirodhasatyaparijñāne / satkāyāntagrāhadṛṣṭibhyāṃ taduttrāsāt [/] mithyādṛṣṭyā cāpavādāt / parāmarśasaṃyojanaṃ mārgasatyaparijñāne / anyathāgraśuddhiparāmarṣaṇāt / vicikitsāsaṃyojanaṃ ratnatrayaparijñāne tadguṇānabhiśraddhānāt / īrṣyāsaṃyojanaṃ lābhasatkāraparijñāne taddoṣādarśanāt / mātsaryasaṃyojanaṃ saṃlekhaparijñāne pariṣkārādhyavasānāt /
body.translated_text: The fetters are obstructions. For the fetter of pride (<s>māna</s>) is an obstruction to the full understanding of the view of the perishable collection. At the time of realization, due to the occurrence of the residual 'I am' conceit (<s>asmīmāna</s>) —

body.text:
[3. Bodhisattvāvaraṇa]
[a. Daśaśubhādiṣv āvaraṇam]
body.translated_text: [3. Obstructions of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] [a. Ten obstructions to wholesome qualities and the like]

children.translated_text: There is another [obstruction], tenfold, to wholesome [qualities] and the like. (II.3)

body.text: aparaṃ punar āvaraṇaṃ / daśavidhe śubhādau veditavyaṃ / kin tad āvaraṇaṃ ke ca śubhādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Another obstruction should be known with regard to the tenfold wholesome [qualities] and the like. What is that obstruction, and what are the wholesome qualities and the like?

children.translated_text: Non-application, [application] in the wrong domain, and improper application;
Non-arising, inattention, incompleteness of the accumulation [of merit and wisdom]; (II.4)
Estrangement from one's spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>) and friends; mental weariness;
Estrangement from practice; and dwelling among corrupt people. (II.5)
Unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), residual [defilements], and immaturity of wisdom from the three [trainings];

children.text: prakṛtyā caiva dauṣṭhulyaṃ kauśīdyaṃ ca pramāditā // II.6
children.translated_text: And natural unsuitability, laziness, and heedlessness; (II.6)

children.text: saktir bhave ca bhoge ca līnacittatvam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Attachment to existence and to enjoyment, and a mind that is withdrawn (<s>līnacittatva</s>);
Lack of faith, lack of resolve, and investigation according to [mere] literal meaning; (II.7)

children.text:
saddharme 'gauravaṃ lābhe gurutā kṛpatā tathā /
śrutavyasanam alpatvaṃ samādhyaparikarmitā // II.8
children.translated_text: Disrespect toward the true <s>Dharma</s>, attachment to gain, miserliness, and also lack of learning, and unpreparedness of <s>samādhi</s>. (II.8)

body.text: etad āvaraṇaṃ / ke śubhādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: This is the obstruction. What are the wholesome qualities and the like?

children.text:
śubhaṃ bodhiḥ samādānan dhīmattvābhrāntyanāvṛtī /
natyatrāso 'matsaritvaṃ vaśitvaṃ ca śubhādayaḥ // II.9
children.translated_text: Wholesome [qualities], awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), undertaking [of vows], wisdom, non-delusion, non-obscuration, fearlessness, non-miserliness, mastery — these are the wholesome qualities and the like. (II.9)

body.text: eṣāṃ śubhādīnāṃ kasya katy āvaraṇāni jñeyānīty āha /
body.translated_text: To explain how many obstructions each of these wholesome qualities and the like has, he says:

body.text: trīṇi trīṇi ca eteṣāṃ jñeyāny āvaraṇāni hi /
body.translated_text: Three obstructions each should be known for these.

body.text: kuśalasya trīṇy āvaraṇāni / aprayogo 'nāyatanaprayogo 'yoniśaḥprayogaś ca / bodhes trīṇi kuśalasyānutpattir amanasikaraṇaṃ / aparipūrṇasaṃbhāratā ca / samādānaṃ bodhicittotpādaḥ / tasya trīṇi gotravaidhuryaṃ kalyāṇamitravaidhuryaṃ / parikhedacittatā ca / dhīmatvaṃ bodhisatvatā / tasyāḥ prajñāne trīṇy āvaraṇāni pratipattivaidhuryaṃ kujanavāsaḥ / duṣṭajanavāsaś ca / tatra kujano mūrkhajanaḥ [/] duṣṭajanaḥ pratihataḥ / abhrāntes trīṇi viparyāsadauṣṭhulyaṃ / kleśādyāvaraṇatrayād anyatamāvaśiṣṭatā / vimuktiparipācinyāḥ (/) prajñāyā aparipakvatā ca / āvaraṇaprahāṇam anāvaraṇaṃ / tasya trīṇi sahajaṃ dauṣṭhulyaṃ / kauśīdyaṃ pramādaś ca / pariṇates trīṇi yair anyatra cittaṃ pariṇāmayati / nānuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau [/]
body.translated_text: Wholesome [qualities] have three obstructions: non-application, application in the wrong domain, and improper application. Awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) has three: non-arising of the wholesome, inattention, and incomplete accumulation.

body.text: bhavasaktir bhogasaktir līnacittatā ca / atrāsasya trīṇi [/] asaṃbhāvanā pudgale / anadhimuktir dharme / yathārutavicāraṇārthe / amātsaryasya trīṇi saddharme 'gauravaṃ / lābhasatkārapūjāyāṃ gauravaṃ satveṣv akāruṇyaṃ ca / vaśitvasya trīṇi yair vibhutvaṃ na labhate [/] śrutavyasanaṃ dharmavyasanasaṃvartanīyakarmaprabhavanāt / alpaśrutatvaṃ / samādher aparikarmitatvaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Attachment to existence, attachment to enjoyment, and a withdrawn mind — [these are the three obstructions] of fearlessness. Of non-miserliness: three — lack of confidence in the person, lack of resolve in the <s>Dharma</s>, and investigation of meaning by mere literal sense.

body.text:
[b. Daśa kāraṇāni]
tat punar etad āvaraṇaṃ śubhādau yatrārthe daśa kāraṇāni tadarthādhikāreṇa veditavyaṃ / daśakāraṇāni [/] utpattikāraṇaṃ tadyathā cakṣurādayaś cakṣurvijñānasya / sthitikāraṇaṃ tad yathā catvāra āhārāḥ satvānāṃ / dhṛtikāraṇaṃ yad yasyādhārabhūtaṃ / tad yathā bhājanalokaḥ satvalokasya / abhivyaktikāraṇaṃ / tad yathā [/] āloko rūpasya / vikārakāraṇaṃ / tad yathāgnyādayaḥ pākyādīnāṃ / viśleṣakāraṇaṃ tad yathā dātrādayaḥ cchedyādīnāṃ / pariṇatikāraṇaṃ / tad yathā suvarṇakārādayaḥ suvarṇādīnāṃ kaṭakādibhāvena pariṇatau / saṃpratyayakāraṇaṃ / tad yathā dhūmādayo 'gnyādīnāṃ / saṃpratyāyanankāraṇaṃ / tad yathā hetuḥ pratijñāyāḥ [/] prāptikāraṇaṃ / tad yathā mārgādayo nirvāṇādīnāṃ /
body.translated_text: [b. Ten causes] Furthermore, this obstruction to the wholesome qualities and the like should be understood in terms of ten causes and their respective domains. The ten causes are: the cause of arising, namely —

body.text: evam utpattyāvaraṇaṃ śubhe draṣṭavyaṃ tasyotpādanīyatvāt / sthityāvaraṇaṃ bodhau tasyā akopyatvād [/] dhṛtyāvaraṇaṃ samādāne bodhicittasyādhārabhūtatvād [/] abhivyaktyāvaraṇaṃ dhīmatve tasya prakāśanīyatvāt / vikārāvaraṇam abhrāntau tasyā (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 32]

children.text: ) bhrāntiparivṛttitvena vikāratvāt / viśleṣāvaraṇam anāvaraṇe tasyāvaraṇavisaṃyogatvāt [/] pariṇatyāvaraṇaṃ natau bodhau cittapariṇatilakṣaṇatvāt / saṃpratyayāvaraṇam atrāse / asaṃpratyayena trasanāt / saṃpratyāyanāvaraṇam amatsaritve dharmāmatsaritvena parasaṃpratyāyanāt / prāptyāvaraṇaṃ vaśitve tasya vibhutvaprāptilakṣaṇatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because of being accompanied by delusion, it undergoes transformation. The obstruction to separation [is seen] in non-obscuration, because [non-obscuration] involves disengagement from obstructions. The obstruction to maturation [is seen] in the bowing to awakening, because it has the character of mental maturation.

body.translated_text: Thus the obstruction to arising should be seen in the wholesome [qualities], because they must be generated. The obstruction to stability [should be seen] in awakening, because it is unshakable. The obstruction to sustaining [should be seen] in the undertaking [of vows], because the <s>bodhicitta</s> is the foundation —

children.translated_text: The ten causes are in: arising, stability, sustaining, illumination,
Transformation, separation, bowing, support, journey, and attainment.
The illustrations for these are: the eye, food, earth, a lamp, fire, and so on;
A sickle, skill, knowledge, smoke, a cause, a path, and the rest.

body.text: bodhiprāptukāmenādita eva tāvat kuśalamūlam utpādayitavyaṃ / tataḥ kuśalamūlabalādhānena bodhiḥ prāptavyā / tasyāḥ punaḥ kuśalamūlotpatter bodhicittaṃ pratiṣṭhā [/] tasya bodhicittasya bodhisatva āśrayaḥ [/] tena punar utpāditabodhicittena kuśalamūlabalādhānaprāptena bodhisatvena viparyāsaṃ prahāya aviparyāsa utpāditavyaḥ / tato darśanamārge 'viparyaste bhāvanāmārge sarvāvaraṇāni prahātavyāni / prahīṇāvaraṇena sarvāṇi kuśalamūlāni anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayitavyāni / tataḥ pariṇāmanābalādhānena gambhīrodāradharmadeśanāsu nottrasitavyaṃ / tathānuttrastamānasena dharmeṣu guṇadarśinā pareṣāṃ te dharmā vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyās [/] tataḥ sa bodhisatva evaṃ vicitraguṇabalādhānaprāptaḥ kṣipram (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 33]

children.text: ) anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim anuprāptavān sarvadharmavaśitām anuprāpnotīty eṣo 'nukramaḥ (/) śubhādīnāṃ [/]
children.translated_text: Having attained unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttaraṃ samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), one attains mastery over all <s>dharmas</s>. This is the sequence of the wholesome qualities and the like.

body.translated_text: One who desires to attain awakening must first of all generate the roots of wholesomeness. Then, through the strengthening of wholesome roots, awakening is to be attained. For the arising of those wholesome roots, the <s>bodhicitta</s> [is needed] —

body.text: [4. Bodhipakṣyapāramitābhūmiṣv āvaraṇam]

children.translated_text: In the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>), the perfections (<s>pāramitās</s>), and the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), there is yet another obstruction. (II.10)

body.translated_text: [4. Obstructions in the <s>bodhipakṣya</s> dharmas, <s>pāramitās</s>, and <s>bhūmis</s>]

body.text:
[a. Bodhipakṣyeṣv āvaraṇam]
bodhipakṣyeṣu tāvat /
body.translated_text: [a. Obstructions in the factors conducive to awakening] First, in the <s>bodhipakṣya</s> dharmas:

children.text:
vastvakauśalakausīdyaṃ samādher dvayahinatā /
aropaṇātha daurbalyaṃ dṛṣṭidauṣṭhulyaduṣṭatā // II.11
children.translated_text: Unskilfulness regarding objects, laziness, deficiency of <s>samādhi</s> in two respects, superimposition, weakness, corruption by views, and unsuitability. (II.11)

body.text: smṛtyupasthāneṣu vastvakauśalam āvaraṇaṃ / samyakprahāṇeṣu kausīdyaṃ [/] ṛddhipādeṣu samādher dvayahīnatā [/] paripūryā ca cchandavīryacittamīmānsānām anyatamavaikalyāt / bhāvanayā ca prahāṇasaṃskāravaikalyāt / indriyeṣu mokṣabhāgīyānām aropaṇaṃ / baleṣu teṣām evendriyāṇāṃ daurbalyaṃ vipakṣavyavakiraṇāt / bodhyaṅgeṣu dṛṣṭidoṣaḥ teṣāṃ darśanamārgaprabhāvitatvāt / mārgāṅgeṣu dauṣṭhulyadoṣaḥ / teṣāṃ bhāvanāmārgaprabhāvitatvāt /
body.translated_text: In the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), unskilfulness regarding objects is the obstruction. In the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), laziness. In the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), deficiency of <s>samādhi</s> in two respects — that is, the incomplete fulfillment of desire, vigor, mind, and investigation —

body.text:
[b. Pāramitāsv āvaraṇam]
pāramitāsv āvaraṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: [b. Obstructions in the perfections] Obstruction in the <s>pāramitās</s>:

children.translated_text: The obscuration of sovereignty, of happy destiny, of not abandoning sentient beings,

children.text: hānivṛddhyoś ca doṣāṇāṃ guṇānām avatāraṇe // II.12
children.translated_text: and of the decrease and increase of faults and virtues, in [their] descent, // II.12

children.text:
vimocane 'kṣayatve ca nairantarye śubhasya ca /
niyatīkaraṇe dharmasaṃbhogaparipācane // II.13
children.translated_text: in liberation, in inexhaustibility, in the continuity of what is auspicious, in making [realization] definite, and in the maturation of the enjoyment of <s>Dharma</s>. // II.13

body.text: atra daśānāṃ pāramitānāṃ yasyāḥ pāramitāyāḥ yat phalaṃ tadāvaraṇena tasyā āvaraṇam udbhāvitaṃ bhavati / tatra dānapāramitāyāḥ aiśvaryādhipatyāvaraṇam āvaraṇaṃ / śīlapāramitāyāḥ sugatyāvaraṇaṃ kṣāntipāramitāyāḥ satvāparityāgāvaraṇaṃ / vīryapāramitāyā doṣaguṇahānivṛddhyāvaraṇaṃ / dhyānapāramitāyā vineyāvatāraṇāvaraṇaṃ / prajñāpāramitāyāḥ vimocanāvaraṇaṃ / upāyakauśalyapāramitāyā dānādyakṣayatvāvaraṇaṃ / bodhipariṇāmanayā tadakṣayatvāt / praṇidhānanpāramitāyāḥ sarvajanmasu kuśalanairantaryapravṛttyāvaraṇaṃ [/] praṇidhānavaśena tadanukūlopapattiparigrahād [[] balapāramitāyās tasyaiva kuśalasya niyatīkaraṇāvaraṇaṃ / pratisaṃkhyānabhāvanābalābhyāṃ vipakṣānabhibhavāt / jñānapāramitāyāḥ ātmaparayor dharmasaṃbhogaparipācanāvaraṇam āvaraṇaṃ / ayathārutaśrutārthāvabodhāt /
body.translated_text: Here, of the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, the obscuration of each <s>pāramitā</s> is indicated by the obscuration of its fruit. The obscuration of the <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (generosity) is the obscuration of sovereignty and mastery. The obscuration of the <s>śīla-pāramitā</s> (morality) is the obscuration of happy destiny. Of the <s>kṣānti-pāramitā</s> (patience), the obscuration of not abandoning sentient beings. Of the <s>vīrya-pāramitā</s> (energy), the obscuration of the decrease and increase of faults and virtues. Of the <s>dhyāna-pāramitā</s> (meditation), the obscuration of the descent [into the world] to train beings. Of the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> (wisdom), the obscuration of liberation. Of the <s>upāyakauśalya-pāramitā</s> (skillful means), the obscuration of the inexhaustibility of generosity and the rest — because through dedication to awakening (<s>bodhipariṇāmanā</s>), these become inexhaustible. Of the <s>praṇidhāna-pāramitā</s> (aspiration), the obscuration of the continuous engagement in virtue in all births — because through aspiration, one takes rebirth in favorable conditions. Of the <s>bala-pāramitā</s> (power), the obscuration of making that very virtue definite — because through the powers of analytical meditation and cultivation, the adversary is not overcome. Of the <s>jñāna-pāramitā</s> (knowledge), the obscuration of the maturation of the enjoyment of <s>Dharma</s> for oneself and others — because one fails to understand the meaning of what is heard according to its literal expression.

body.text:
[c. Bhūmiṣv āvaraṇam]
bhūmiṣu punar yathākramaṃ /
body.translated_text: [c. Obscuration at the <s>Bhūmis</s> (Stages)] Furthermore, at the [ten] stages, in order:

body.text: sarvatragārthe agrārthe niṣyandāgrārtha eva ca /
body.translated_text: In the meaning of omnipresence, in the meaning of preeminence, in the meaning of preeminence of outflow,

children.text: niṣparigrahatārthe ca santānābheda eva ca // II.14
children.translated_text: and in the meaning of non-attachment, and in the non-splitting of the continuum, // II.14
in the meaning of the purity free from affliction, in the meaning of non-diversity,
in the meaning of neither deficiency nor excess, and in the four masteries as the basis, // II.15

children.text:
dharmadhātāv avidyeyaṃ akliṣṭā daśadhāvṛtiḥ /
daśabhūmivipakṣeṇa pratipakṣās tu bhūmayaḥ // II.16
children.translated_text: this unafflicted ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharmas</s>) is a tenfold obscuration; the [ten] stages are the antidote to the ten-stage adversary. // II.16

body.text: dharmadhātau daśavidhe sarvatragādyarthe yad akliṣṭam ajñānaṃ tad daśasu bodhisatvabhūmiṣv āvaraṇaṃ yathākramaṃ tadvipakṣatvāt / yad uta
body.translated_text: The unafflicted ignorance regarding the <s>dharmadhātu</s> in its ten aspects — the meaning of omnipresence and so forth — is the obscuration at the ten <s>bodhisattva</s> stages in order, since it is their adversary. Namely:

body.text: sarvatragārthe
body.translated_text: Regarding the meaning of omnipresence —

body.text: prathamayā hi bhūmyā dharmadhātoḥ sarvatragārthaṃ pratividhyati [/] yenātmaparasamatāṃ pratilabhate / dvitīyayāgrārthaṃ [/] yenāsyaivaṃ bhavati tasmāt tarhy asmābhiḥ samāne 'bhinirhāre sarvākārapariśodhanābhinirhāra eva yogaḥ karaṇīya iti / tṛtīyayā tanniṣyandāgrārthaṃ / yena dharmadhātuniṣyandasya śrutasyāgratāṃ viditvā tadarthaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrapramāṇāyām apy agnikhadāyām ātmānaṃ prakṣipet / caturthyā niṣparigrahatārthan tathā hi dharmatṛṣṇāpi vyāvartate / pañcamyā santānābhedārthaṃ daśabhiś cittāśayaviśuddhisamatābhiḥ / ṣaṣṭhyā niḥsaṃkleṣaviśuddhyarthaṃ pratītyasamutpāde (/) nāsti sa kaścid dharmo yaḥ saṃkliśyate vā viśudhyate veti prativedhāt / saptamyānānātvārthaṃ nirnimittatayā sūtrādidharmanimittanānātvāsamudācārād [/] aṣṭamyāhīnānadhikārtham anutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhāt saṃkleśe vyavadāne vā (

children.translated_text: <s>Mvbh</s> 36

children.text: ) kasyacid dharmasya hānivṛddhyadarśanāc [/] caturdhā vaśitā nirvikalpavaśitā kṣetrapariśuddhivaśitā jñānavaśitā karmavaśitā ca [/] tatra prathamadvitīyavaśitāśrayatvaṃ dharmadhātāv aṣṭamyaiva bhūmyā pratividdhati / jñānavaśitāśrayatvaṃ navamyāṃ pratisaṃvillābhāt / karmavaśitāśrayatvaṃ daśamyāṃ yathecchaṃ nirmāṇaiḥ satvārthakaraṇāt /
children.translated_text: The four masteries are: mastery over non-conceptualization, mastery over the purification of [Buddha-]fields, mastery over knowledge, and mastery over action. Of these, the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is penetrated as the basis of the first and second masteries by the eighth stage itself. The basis of mastery over knowledge [is penetrated] at the ninth, through the obtaining of analytical knowledge (<s>pratisaṃvit</s>). The basis of mastery over action [is penetrated] at the tenth, through acting for the welfare of beings by means of emanations as one wishes.

body.translated_text: By the first stage, one penetrates the omnipresent meaning of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, whereby one obtains the equality of self and other. By the second, the meaning of preeminence, whereby one resolves: 'Therefore, since we are equal in endeavor, the effort should be made toward the endeavor of purification in every aspect.' By the third, the meaning of the preeminence of its outflow, whereby, knowing the preeminence of what is heard as the outflow of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, one would throw oneself into a pit of fire the size of a great trichiliocosm for the sake of that. By the fourth, the meaning of non-attachment — for even attachment to the <s>Dharma</s> is turned away. By the fifth, the meaning of the non-splitting of the continuum — through the ten equalities of the purification of mental disposition. By the sixth, the meaning of the purity free from affliction — through the penetration that in dependent origination, there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that is defiled or purified. By the seventh, the meaning of non-diversity — through the non-engagement in the diversity of marks of <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>sūtras</s>, due to the absence of marks. By the eighth, the meaning of neither deficiency nor excess — through obtaining the <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patience with the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>), seeing neither decrease nor increase of any <s>dharma</s> in defilement or purification.

body.text:
[5. Avaraṇasamāsa]
samāsena punaḥ /
body.translated_text: [5. Summary of Obscurations] In summary:

children.text:
kleśāvaraṇam ākhyātaṃ jñeyāvaraṇam eva ca /
sarvāṇy āvaraṇānīha yatkṣayān muktir iṣyate // II.17
children.translated_text: The obscuration of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) are declared; liberation is held to result from the destruction of all obscurations here. // II.17

body.text: asya hi dvividhasyāvaraṇasya (/) kṣayāt sarvāvaraṇebhyo muktir iṣyate /
body.translated_text: From the destruction of this twofold obscuration, liberation from all obscurations is held to result.

body.text:
[Āvaraṇapiṇḍārtha]
āvaraṇānāṃ piṇḍārthaḥ / mahad āvaraṇaṃ yad vyāpi / pratanv āvaraṇaṃ yat prādeśikaṃ / prayogāvaraṇaṃ yad udriktaṃ / prāptyāvaraṇaṃ yat samaṃ / prāptiviśeṣāvaraṇaṃ yad ādānavivarjane / samyakprayogāvaraṇaṃ yan navadhākleśāvaraṇaṃ / hetvāvaraṇaṃ yac chubhādau daśavidhahetvarthādhikārāt i tatvapraveśāvaraṇaṃ yad bodhipakṣyeṣu / śubhānuttaryāvaraṇaṃ yat pāramitāsu / tadviśeṣagatyāvaraṇaṃ yad bhūmiṣu / saṃgrahāvaraṇaṃ yat samāsato dvividhaṃ //
body.translated_text: [Condensed Meaning of Obscurations] The condensed meaning of the obscurations: A great obscuration is one that is all-pervading. A subtle obscuration is one that is localized. An obscuration of practice is one that is predominant. An obscuration of attainment is one that is moderate. An obscuration of the distinction of attainment concerns the abandonment of grasping. An obscuration of correct practice is the ninefold affliction-obscuration. A causal obscuration concerns the ten kinds of causal purposes in virtue and so forth. An obscuration of penetrating reality concerns the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>). An obscuration of the unsurpassed in virtue concerns the <s>pāramitās</s>. An obscuration of the path to the distinction thereof concerns the stages. A summary obscuration is the twofold [obscuration] in brief. //

body.text: madhyāntavibhāge āvaraṇaparicchedo dvitīyaḥ // ḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Madhyāntavibhāga</s>, the second chapter, on obscuration (<s>āvaraṇapariccheda</s>). //

body.text:
[CHAPTER III. TATTVAPARICCHEDA]
tatvam adhikṛtyāha /
body.translated_text: [CHAPTER III. CHAPTER ON REALITY (<s>TATTVAPARICCHEDA</s>)] Regarding reality (<s>tattva</s>), [the text] says:

children.translated_text: The root-reality, the characteristic-reality,

children.text: phalahetumayan tatvaṃ sūkṣmaudārikam eva ca // III. 1
children.translated_text: the non-inversion reality, the fruit-and-cause reality, the subtle and the gross, // III.1

children.text:
prasiddhaṃ śuddhiviṣayaṃ saṃgrāhyaṃ bhedalakṣaṇaṃ /
kauśalyatatvaṃ daśadhā ātmadṛṣṭivipakṣataḥ // III.2
children.translated_text: the well-known, the object of purification, the comprehensive, the distinctive, and the skill-reality — tenfold, as the antidote to the view of self. // III.2

body.text: ity etad daśavidhaṃ tatvaṃ yad uta mūlatatvaṃ lakṣaṇatatvaṃ / aviparyāsatatvaṃ / phalahetutatvaṃ / audārikasūkṣmatatvaṃ / prasiddhatatvaṃ / viśuddhigocaratatvaṃ / saṃgrahatatvaṃ] prabhedatatvaṃ / kauśalyatatvañ ca / tat punar daśavidhaṃ daśavidhātmagrāhapratipakṣeṇa veditavyaṃ / tad yathā skandhakauśalyaṃ / dhātukauśalyam āyatanakauśalyaṃ / pratītyasamutpādakauśalyaṃ / sthānāsthānakauśalyam indriyakauśalyaṃ adhvakauśalyaṃ satyakauśalyaṃ yānakauśalyaṃ / saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtakauśalyaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Thus this reality is tenfold: root-reality, characteristic-reality, non-inversion reality, fruit-and-cause reality, gross-and-subtle reality, well-known reality, purification-domain reality, comprehensive reality, distinctive reality, and skill-reality. Furthermore, this tenfold [reality] should be understood as the antidote to the tenfold grasping of self. Namely: skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), skill in the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), skill in the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), skill in dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), skill in what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthāna</s>), skill in the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), skill in time-periods, skill in the truths (<s>satya</s>), skill in the vehicles (<s>yāna</s>), and skill in the conditioned and unconditioned.

body.text:
[1. Mūlatattva]
tatra mūlatatvaṃ /
body.translated_text: [1. Root-Reality] Therein, the root-reality:

children.translated_text: The [three] natures (<s>svabhāvas</s>) are threefold:

body.text: parikalpitaḥ paratantraḥ pariniṣpannaś ca / tatrānyatatvavyavasthāpanāt / kim atra svabhāvatraye tatvam iṣyate /
body.translated_text: the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>), the other-dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), and the consummate (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>). By the establishment of the otherness of these [from what they appear to be] — what is held to be reality in this threefold nature?

children.text:
asac ca nityaṃ sac cāpy atatvataḥ
sadasattatvataś ceti svabhāvatraya iṣyate // III.3
children.translated_text: The non-existent is always existent too, but not in reality; in terms of the existent and non-existent in reality — thus [reality] is held in the three natures. // III.3

body.text: parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ nityam asad ity etat parikalpitasvabhāve tatvam aviparītatvāt [/] paratantralakṣaṇaṃ sac ca na ca tatvato bhrāntatvād ity etat paratantrasvabhāve tatvaṃ / pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ sadasattatvataś cety etat (/) pariniṣpannasvabhāve tatvaṃ /
body.translated_text: The imagined nature is always non-existent — this is the reality of the imagined nature, because it is not mistaken. The other-dependent nature is existent, but not in reality, because it is deluded — this is the reality of the other-dependent nature. The consummate nature is existent and non-existent in reality — this is the reality of the consummate nature.

body.text:
[2. Laksaṇatattva]
lakṣaṇatatvaṃ katamat /
body.translated_text: [2. Characteristic-Reality] What is the characteristic-reality?

children.translated_text: The perception of superimposition and deprecation regarding <s>dharmas</s> and persons,

children.text: grāhyagrāhakayoś cāpi bhāvābhāve ca darśanaṃ // III.4
children.translated_text: and regarding the grasped and grasper, and in existence and non-existence — // III.4

children.text: yajjñānān na pravarteta tad dhi tatvasya lakṣaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: that which does not arise from [correct] knowledge — that is the characteristic of reality.

body.text: pudgaladharmayoḥ samāropāpavādadarśanaṃ yasya jñānān na pravartate / tat parikalpitasvabhāve tatvalakṣaṇaṃ / grāhyagrāhakayoḥ samāropāpavādadarśanaṃ yasya jñānān na pravartate / tat paratantrasvabhāve tatvalakṣaṇaṃ / bhāvābhāvasamāropāpavādadarśanaṃ yasya jñānān na pravartate / tat pariniṣpannasvabhāve tatvalakṣaṇaṃ / etan mūlatatve lakṣaṇam aviparītaṃ lakṣaṇatatvam ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: That from whose knowledge the perception of superimposition and deprecation regarding persons and <s>dharmas</s> does not arise — that is the characteristic of reality in the imagined nature. That from whose knowledge the perception of superimposition and deprecation regarding the grasped and grasper does not arise — that is the characteristic of reality in the other-dependent nature. That from whose knowledge the perception of superimposition and deprecation regarding existence and non-existence does not arise — that is the characteristic of reality in the consummate nature. This, being the non-erroneous characteristic of the root-reality, is called the characteristic-reality.

body.text:
[3. Aviparyāsatattva]
aviparyāsatatvaṃ nityādiviparyāsapratipakṣeṇānityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmatā mūlatatve yathākramaṃ [/] kathaṃ ca tatrānityatāditā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: [3. Non-Inversion Reality] The non-inversion reality [is:] as the antidote to the inversions of permanence and so forth, impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self in the root-reality in order. And how are impermanence and the rest to be understood therein?

children.translated_text: The meaning of non-existent is indeed the meaning of impermanent, characterized by arising and cessation. // III.5
In the root-reality, in order, [there is] the state of being with defilement and the state of being without defilement.

body.text: trayo hi svabhāvā mūlatatvaṃ [/] teṣu yathākramam
body.translated_text: The three natures are the root-reality. In them, in order:

body.text: asadartho hy anityārtha
body.translated_text: 'The meaning of non-existent is indeed the meaning of impermanent' —

body.text: utpādavyayārthaḥ samalāmalatārthaś ca /
body.translated_text: the meaning of arising and cessation, and the meaning of being with and without defilement.

children.translated_text: Suffering is said to be characterized by appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>), by mark, and by connection. // III.6

body.text: mūlatatve yathākramaṃ duḥkham upādānataḥ pudgaladharmābhiniveśopādānāt / lakṣaṇatas triduḥkhatālakṣaṇatvāt / saṃbandhataś ca duḥkhasaṃbandhāt [/] tatraiva mūlatatve yathākramaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: In the root-reality, in order: suffering through appropriation — from the appropriation of grasping at persons and <s>dharmas</s>; suffering through mark — from being characterized by the three kinds of suffering; and suffering through connection — from connection with suffering. This is to be understood in the root-reality in order.

body.text: abhāvaś cāpy atadbhāvaḥ prakṛtiḥ śūnyatā matā /
body.translated_text: Non-existence, the state of not-being-that, and the essential nature — these are held to be emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>).

body.text: parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ na kenacit prakāreṇāstīty abhāva evāsya śūnyatā paratantralakṣaṇaṃ tathā nāsti yathā parikalpyate na tu sarvathā nāstīti tasyātadbhāvaḥ (/) śūnyatā [/] pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ śūnyatāsvabhāvam eveti prakṛtir evāsya śūnyatā /
body.translated_text: The characteristic of the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>) does not exist in any manner whatsoever — thus its emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is simply non-existence. The characteristic of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) does not exist as it is imagined, but it is not entirely non-existent — thus its emptiness is the absence of that [imagined nature].

children.text: alakṣaṇaṃ ca nairātmyaṃ tadvilakṣaṇam eva ca // III.7
children.translated_text: Non-characterization (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>) is [one form of] selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), and different-characterization (<s>vilakṣaṇa</s>) [is another]; (III.7)
And own-characterization (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is also taught.

body.text: parikalpitasya svabhāvasya lakṣaṇam eva nāstīty alakṣaṇam evāsya nairātmyaṃ [/] paratantrasyāsti lakṣaṇaṃ na tu yathā parikalpyata iti tadvilakṣaṇam asya lakṣaṇan nairātmyaṃ / pariniṣpannas tu svabhāvo nairātmyam eveti prakṛtir evāsya nairātmyam iti trividhe mūlatatve trividhānityatā paridīpitā asadarthānityatā utpādabhaṅgānityatā samalanirmalānityatā ca / trividhā duḥkhatā upādānaduḥkhatā lakṣaṇaduḥkhatā saṃbandhaduḥkhatā (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 40]

children.text: ) ca / trividhā śūnyatā abhāvaśūnyatā atadbhāvaśūnyatā svabhāvaśūnyatā ca trividhaṃ nairātmyaṃ alakṣaṇanairātmyaṃ / vilakṣaṇanairātmyaṃ svalakṣaṇanairātmyaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Thus there is a threefold emptiness: emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of the absence of that [nature], and emptiness of own-nature. And threefold selflessness: selflessness of non-characterization, selflessness of different-characterization, and selflessness of own-characterization.

body.translated_text: The selflessness of the imagined nature is that it has no characterization at all — it is simply non-characterization (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>). The dependent has characterization, but not as it is imagined — thus its selflessness is different-characterization (<s>vilakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text:
[4. Phalahetutattva]
phalahetumayan tatvaṃ tatraiva mūlatatve duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgasatyatvaṃ [/] kathaṃ trividhaṃ mūlatatvaṃ duḥkhādisatyatvaṃ [/] yatas tad anityādilakṣaṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: [4. The truth of result and cause (<s>phalahetutatva</s>)] The truth of result and cause, within the root truth, is the truth of suffering, origination, cessation, and path. How is the threefold root truth the truth of suffering and so forth?

children.translated_text: Suffering-truth is understood from this.

body.text: trividhena samudayārthena samudayasatyaṃ [/] trividhaḥ samudayārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Origination-truth is [understood] by means of a threefold meaning of origination. The threefold meaning of origination:

children.text: vāsanātha samutthānam avisaṃyoga eva ca // III.8
children.translated_text: Latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), arising, and non-separation as well. (III.8)

body.text: vāsanāsamudayaḥ parikalpitasvabhāvābhiniveśavāsanā samutthānasamudayaḥ karmakleśāḥ / avisaṃyogasamudayaḥ / tathatāyā āvaraṇāvisaṃyogaḥ / trividhena nirodhena nirodhasatyaṃ [/] trividho nirodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: The origination of latent impressions is the latent impression of clinging to the imagined nature. The origination of arising is <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). The origination of non-separation is the non-separation of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) from obstructions. By means of a threefold cessation —

body.text: svabhāvadvayanotpattir malaśāntidvayaṃ mataṃ /
body.translated_text: Non-arising of the two natures, and two [aspects of] purification from defilement are taught.

body.text: svabhāvānutpattir grāhyagrāhakayor anutpattir malaśāntidvayaṃ ca pratisaṃkhyānirodhatathatākhyam ity eṣa trividho nirodho yad uta svabhāvanirodho dvayanirodhaḥ / prakṛtinirodhaś ca / mārgasatyaṃ trividhe mūlatatve kathaṃ vyavasthāpyate /
body.translated_text: Non-arising of own-nature, non-arising of the grasped and grasper, and the two [aspects of] purification from defilement — namely, analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) and that called <s>tathatā</s> — this is the threefold cessation: cessation of own-nature, cessation of the two, and [cessation through] purification.

children.text: parijñāyāṃ prahāṇe ca prāptisākṣātkṛtāv ayaṃ [//] III.9
children.translated_text: In full understanding, abandonment, and attainment-realization — this (III.9)
Is declared to be the path-truth.

body.text: parikalpitasya parijñāne paratantrasya parijñāne prahāṇe ca / pariniṣpannasya parijñāne prāptisākṣātkaraṇe ca evam atra parijñāprahāṇasākṣātkriyāyāṃ mārgasatyavyavasthānam iti veditavyaṃ [/]
body.translated_text: In the full understanding of the imagined, in the full understanding and abandonment of the dependent, and in the full understanding, attainment, and direct realization of the consummate (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) — thus, here, in full understanding, abandonment, and direct realization, the path —

body.text:
[5. Audārikasūkṣmatattva]
audārikasūkṣmatatvaṃ punaḥ saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyaṃ tan mūlatatve kathaṃ veditavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: [5. The truth of the coarse and subtle (<s>audārikasūkṣmatatva</s>)] Furthermore, the truth of the coarse and subtle — the conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) and ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) truths — how is it to be known in the root truth?

children.translated_text: Through designation and engagement, and likewise through manifestation, [the conventional is known as] coarse.

body.text: trividhā hi saṃvṛtiḥ prajñaptisaṃvṛtiḥ / pratipattisaṃvṛtiḥ / udbhāvanāsaṃvṛtiś ca / tayā saṃvṛtisatyatvaṃ mūlatatve yathākramaṃ veditavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: For the conventional is threefold: the conventional of designation, the conventional of engagement, and the conventional of manifestation. Through that conventional [truth], the truth of the conventional in the root truth should be known in their respective order.

children.translated_text: But the ultimate is from one [alone]. (III.10)

body.text: paramārthasatyaṃ / ekasmāt pariniṣpannād eva svabhāvād veditavyaṃ / sa punaḥ kathaṃ paramārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: The ultimate truth should be known from the consummate nature alone. How is it ultimate?

body.text: arthaprāptiprapattyā hi paramārthas tridhā mataḥ /
body.translated_text: The ultimate is regarded as threefold: through meaning, attainment, and practice.

body.text: arthaparamārthas tathatā paramasya jñānasyārtha iti kṛtvā / prāptiparamārtho nirvāṇaṃ paramo 'rtha iti kṛtvā pratipattiparamārtho mārgaḥ paramo 'syārtha iti kṛtvā [/] katham asaṃskṛtaṃ ca (/) saṃskṛtaṃ ca (/) pariniṣpannaḥ (/) svabhāva ucyate /
body.translated_text: The ultimate as meaning: <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — because it is the object of the supreme knowledge. The ultimate as attainment: <s>nirvāṇa</s> — because it is the supreme goal. The ultimate as practice: the path — because its goal is supreme.

children.translated_text: Through non-modification and non-error, the consummate is twofold. (III.11)

body.text: asaṃskṛtam avikārapariniṣpattyā pariniṣpannaṃ / saṃskṛtaṃ mārgasatyasaṃgṛhītam aviparyāsapariniṣpattyā punar jñeyavastuny (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 42]
due to non-error.

body.translated_text: The unconditioned is consummate through the consummation of non-modification. The conditioned, included in path-truth, is [consummate] through the consummation of non-error — regarding the knowable object,

body.text:
[6. Prasiddhatattva]
prasiddhatatvaṃ mūlatatve kathaṃ vyavasthāpyate / dvividhaṃ hi prasiddhatatvaṃ / lokaprasiddhaṃ yuktiprasiddhaṃ ca / tatra /
body.translated_text: [6. The truth of the well-known (<s>prasiddhatatva</s>)] How is the truth of the well-known established in the root truth? The truth of the well-known is twofold: well-known to the world and well-known to reasoning. Therein:

children.translated_text: That which is well-known to the world is from one [nature] —

body.text: parikalpitasvabhāvāt / yasmin vastuni saṃketasaṃstavānupraviṣṭayā buddhyā sarveṣāṃ laukikānāṃ darśanatulyatā bhavati / pṛthivy eveyaṃ nāgnī rūpam evedaṃ na śabda ity evamādi /
body.translated_text: From the imagined nature. Regarding whatever object, through a cognition that has entered into conventional agreement and familiar usage, there is sameness of view among all worldly beings: 'This is surely earth, not fire; this is surely form, not [something else]' —

body.text: trayād yuktiprasiddhakaṃ /
body.translated_text: That which is well-known to reasoning is from [all] three.

body.text: yat satāṃ yuktārthapaṇḍitānāṃ tārkikāṇāṃ pramāṇatrayaṃ niśrityopapattisādhanayuktyā prasiddhaṃ vastu /
body.translated_text: Whatever object is well-known to the wise, the learned in correct reasoning, the logicians, through reliance on the three means of valid knowledge and through the reasoning that establishes cogency.

body.text:
[7. Viśuddhigocaratattva]
viśuddhigocaratatvaṃ dvividhaṃ kleśāvaraṇaviśuddhijñānagocaraṃ / jñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhijñānagocaraṃ ca / tad etat /
body.translated_text: [7. The truth of the domain of purification (<s>viśuddhiśdocaratatva</s>)] The truth of the domain of purification is twofold: the domain of the knowledge purified of the obstruction of afflictions, and the domain of the knowledge purified of the obstruction of the knowable. This:

children.text: viśuddhigocaraṃ dvedhā ekasmād eva kīrtitaṃ // III.12
children.translated_text: The domain of purification is said to be twofold, from one [nature] alone. (III.12)

body.text: pariniṣpannād eva svabhāvān na hy anyasvabhāvo viśuddhijñānadvayagocaro bhavati /
body.translated_text: From the consummate nature alone — for no other nature can be the domain of the two kinds of purified knowledge.

body.text:
[8. Saṃgrahatattva]
kathaṃ trividhe mūlatatve saṃgrahatatvaṃ veditavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: [8. The truth of inclusion (<s>saṃgrahatatva</s>)] How is the truth of inclusion to be known in the threefold root truth?

body.text: nimittasya vikalpasya nāmnaś ca dvayasaṃgrahaḥ /
body.translated_text: The inclusion of the sign (<s>nimitta</s>), conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>), and name (<s>nāman</s>) is twofold.

body.text: yathāyogaṃ pañca vastūny ārabhya nimittavikalpayoḥ paratantreṇa (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 43]
and the inclusion of name is [within] the imagined.

body.translated_text: With respect to the five objects, as appropriate, the inclusion of sign and conceptualization is [within] the dependent,

children.translated_text: And the inclusion of right knowledge and suchness is by one [nature] alone. (III.13)

body.text: tathatāsamyagjñānayoḥ pariniṣpannena svabhāvena saṃgrahaḥ /
body.translated_text: The inclusion of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and right knowledge is by the consummate nature.

body.text:
[9. Prabhedatattva]
prabhedatatvaṃ mūlatatve kathaṃ veditavyaṃ / saptavidhaṃ prabhedatatvaṃ pravṛttitatvaṃ / lakṣaṇatatvaṃ / vijñaptitatvaṃ sanniveśatatvaṃ / mithyāpratipattitatvaṃ / viśuddhitatvaṃ samyakpratipattitatvañ ca / (tatra pravṛttitatvāditrividhaṃ / anavarāgreṣv eti saṃsāraḥ tathatācittasaṃkleśāt satvāḥ saṃkliśyanta iti sarvaṃ duḥkhādisatyaṃ ca yathāsaṃkhyaṃ) yaiva ca sandhinirmocanasūtre saptavidhā tathatā nirdiṣṭā / tatra /
body.translated_text: [9. The truth of differentiation (<s>prabhedatatva</s>)] How is the truth of differentiation to be known in the root truth? The truth of differentiation is sevenfold: the truth of activity, the truth of characteristics, the truth of cognition, the truth of configuration —

body.text: pravṛttitatvaṃ dvividhaṃ /
body.translated_text: The truth of activity is twofold.

body.text: mūlatatvaṃ veditavyaṃ / parikalpitaparatantralakṣaṇaṃ / yathā pravṛttitatvaṃ tathā /
body.translated_text: The root truth should be known as having the imagined and dependent characteristics. Just as [it applies to] the truth of activity, so also —

body.text: sanniveśakupannatā /
body.translated_text: Configuration and wrong engagement.

body.text: sanniveśamithyāpratipattitatve api tathaiva dvividhaṃ mūlatatvaṃ /
body.translated_text: In the truth of configuration and wrong engagement too, the root truth is likewise twofold.

children.translated_text: But one [nature underlies] characterization, cognition, purification, and right engagement. (III.14)

body.text: lakṣaṇatatvādīni catvāry ekaṃ mūlatatvaṃ pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: The four [truths] beginning with characterization are one root truth — the consummate characteristic.

body.text:
[10. Kauśalyatattva]
kauśalyatatvaṃ darśanapratipakṣeṇety uktaṃ / katham eṣu skandhādiṣu daśavidham ātmadarśanam /

children.translated_text: As oneness, cause, enjoyer, agent, controller,
Master, purposeful, permanent, and as the basis of affliction and purification. (III.15)
And as yogi and as liberated-and-unliberated — the view of self in these indeed.
