body.translated_text: [10. The truth of skill (<s>kauśalyatatva</s>)] The truth of skill is said to be through the antidote to [wrong] views. How is the tenfold view of self in the aggregates and the like?

body.text: eṣa daśavidha ātmāsadgrāhaḥ skandhādiṣu pravartate / yasya pratipakṣeṇa daśavidhaṃ kauśalyaṃ yad utaikatvagrāho hetutvagrāho bhoktṛtvagrāhaḥ / kartṛtvagrāhaḥ / svatantragrāhaḥ i adhipatitvagrāho nityatvagrāhaḥ / saṃkliṣṭavyavadānatvagrāho yogitvagrāhaḥ / amuktamuktatvagrāhaś ca /
body.translated_text: This tenfold false grasping of self operates in the aggregates and the like. The skill that counteracts it is tenfold: the grasping of oneness, the grasping of being a cause, the grasping of being an enjoyer, the grasping of being an agent —

body.text: katham idaṃ daśavidhaṃ kauśalyatatvaṃ mūlatatve 'ntarbhavati / yatas triṣu svabhāveṣu te skandhādayo 'ntarbhūtāḥ / katham antarbhūtāḥ /
body.translated_text: How does this tenfold truth of skill fall within the root truth? Because those aggregates and the like are included within the three natures. How are they included?

children.translated_text: Through the meanings of imagining, conceptualization, object, and <s>dharmatā</s>, they [are included] in those. (III.16)

body.text: trividhaṃ rūpaṃ parikalpitaṃ rūpaṃ yo rūpasya parikalpitaḥ svabhāvaḥ / vikalpitaṃ rūpaṃ yo rūpasya paratantraḥ (/) svabhāvas tatra hi rūpavikalpaḥ kriyate / dharmatārūpaṃ yo rūpasya pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvaḥ / yathā rūpam evaṃ vedanādayaḥ skandhāḥ dhātvāyatanādayaś ca yojyāḥ / evan triṣu svabhāveṣu skandhādīnām antarbhāvād daśavidhaṃ kauśalyatatvaṃ mūlatatva eva draṣṭavyaṃ / uktam idaṃ yathā daśavidhātmadarśanapratipakṣeṇa skandhādikauśalyaṃ [/] skandhādyarthas tu noktaḥ / sa idānīm ucyate/
body.translated_text: Form is threefold: imagined form — that which is the imagined nature of form; conceptualized form — that which is the dependent nature of form, for therein the conceptualization of form operates —

body.text: [a. Skandhārtha]

children.translated_text: From the beginning, [the aggregates are taught] for the purposes of multiplicity, condensation, and delimitation.

body.translated_text: [a. The meaning of the aggregates (<s>skandhārtha</s>)]

body.text: āditas tāvat skandhās te trividhenārthena veditavyāḥ / anekatvārthena yat kiñcid rūpam atītānāgatapratyutpannam iti vistaraḥ / abhisaṃkṣepārthena tat sarvam aikadhyam abhisaṃkṣipyeti / paricchedārthena ca rūpādilakṣaṇasya pṛthaktvavyavasthānāt / rāśyartho hi skandhārtha evaṃ ca loke rāśyartho dṛṣṭa iti /
body.translated_text: First, the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) are to be understood in three senses: in the sense of multiplicity — 'whatever form, past, future, or present' and so forth in detail; in the sense of summarization — 'all that is compressed into one'; and in the sense of delimitation — because of the separate establishment of the characteristics of form and the rest. For the meaning of 'aggregate' (<s>skandha</s>) is 'heap' (<s>rāśi</s>), and thus the meaning of 'heap' is seen in the world.

body.text: [b. Dhātvartha]

children.translated_text: Another [category] is regarded as having the meaning of the seed of the apprehender, the apprehended, and the apprehension thereof. // III. 17

body.translated_text: [b. The meaning of <s>dhātu</s> (element)]

body.text: katamo 'paro dhātus tatra grāhakabījārthaḥ cakṣurdhātvādayaḥ [/] grāhyabījārtho rūpadhātvādayas [/] tadgrāhabījārthaś cakṣurvijñānadhātvādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the other [category], the <s>dhātu</s>? Therein, those having the meaning of the seed of the apprehender are the eye-element (<s>cakṣurdhātu</s>) and so forth. Those having the meaning of the seed of the apprehended are the form-element (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) and so forth. Those having the meaning of the seed of the apprehension thereof are the eye-consciousness-element (<s>cakṣurvijñānadhātu</s>) and so forth.

body.text: [c. Āyatanārtha]

children.translated_text: Another [category is understood] from [its being] a gateway to the experience of the knower and the delimitation of the object.

body.translated_text: [c. The meaning of <s>āyatana</s> (sense-base)]

body.text: kim aparaṃ āyatanaṃ / tatra veditopabhogāyadvārārthena ṣaḍ ādhyātmikāny āyatanāni / arthaparicchedopabhogāyadvārārthena ṣaḍ bāhyāni /
body.translated_text: What is the other — the <s>āyatana</s>? Therein, the six internal sense-bases are [understood] in the sense of being gateways to the experience of the knower. The six external [sense-bases are understood] in the sense of being gateways to the experience of the delimitation of objects.

body.text:
[d. Pratītyasamutpādārtha]
pratītyasamutpādārthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
[d. The meaning of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination)]
The meaning of dependent origination:

children.translated_text: Furthermore, from the [avoidance of] superimposition and denial regarding cause, effect, and action — // III.18

body.text: hetuphalakriyāṇām asamāropānapavādārthaḥ pratītyasamutpādārthaḥ / tatra hetu sa nāropaḥ saṃskārādīnāṃ viṣamahetukalpanāt / (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 46]

children.text: ) hetvapavādo nirhetukatvakalpanāt phalasamāropaḥ sātmakānāṃ saṃskārādīnām avidyādipratyayapravṛttikalpanāt / phalāpavādo na santy avidyādipratyayāḥ saṃskārādaya iti kalpanāt / kriyāsamāropo 'vidyādīnāṃ saṃskārādyutpattau vyāpārakalpanāt kriyāpavādo niḥsāmarthyakalpanāt tadabhāvād asamāropānapavādo veditavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The denial of a cause is the fabrication that [things are] without cause. The superimposition of an effect is the fabrication that <s>saṃskāras</s> and the rest, which possess a self, operate through the condition of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and so forth. The denial of an effect is the fabrication that 'the conditions such as ignorance do not exist, [and therefore] formations and the rest [do not exist].' The superimposition of action is the fabrication that ignorance and the rest perform an operation in the production of formations and the rest. The denial of action is the fabrication that [causes] have no efficacy. Due to the absence of these [errors], [dependent origination] should be understood as non-superimposition and non-denial.

body.translated_text: The meaning of dependent origination is the non-superimposition and non-denial of causes, effects, and actions. Therein, the superimposition of a cause is the fabrication of a dissimilar cause for <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) and the rest.

body.text: [e. Sthānāsthānārtha]

children.translated_text: Of the undesirable, the desirable, and purification, with respect to [their] co-arising and sovereignty — from the meaning of dependence regarding attainment and occurrence, another [category is understood]. // III. 19

body.translated_text: [e. The meaning of <s>sthānāsthāna</s> (the possible and the impossible)]

body.text: sthānāsthānaṃ saptavidhapāratantryārthena veditavyaṃ / tatrāniṣṭe pāratantryaṃ duścaritenānicchato 'pi durgatigamanād iṣṭe pāratantryaṃ sucaritena sugatigamanāt / viśuddhau pāratantryaṃ pañca nivaraṇāny aprahāya yāvat saptabodhyaṅgāny abhāvayitvā duḥkhasyāntākaraṇāt samotpattau pāratantryaṃ dvayor apūrvācaramayos tathāgatayoś cakravartinoś caikasmin lokadhātāv anutpādād ādhipatye pāratantryaṃ striyāś cakravartitvādyakaraṇāt saṃprāptau pāratantryaṃ striyāḥ pratyekānuttarabodhyanabhisaṃbodhāt samudācāre pāratantryaṃ dṛṣṭisaṃpannasya vadhādyupakramāsamudācārāt pṛthagjanasya ca samudācārād vistareṇa bahudhātukasūtrānusārād anugantavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>Sthānāsthāna</s> (the possible and the impossible) is to be understood in the sense of sevenfold dependence. Therein, dependence regarding the undesirable [means] going to a bad destiny unwillingly through bad conduct. Dependence regarding the desirable [means] going to a good destiny through good conduct. Dependence regarding purification [means] not being able to make an end of suffering without abandoning the five hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇas</s>) and without cultivating the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>). Dependence regarding co-arising [means] that two <s>Tathāgatas</s> or two <s>Cakravartins</s>, unprecedented and not final, do not arise in a single world-system. Dependence regarding sovereignty [means] that a woman cannot become a <s>Cakravartin</s> and so forth. Dependence regarding attainment [means] that a woman cannot attain <s>Pratyeka</s>- or supreme awakening. Dependence regarding occurrence [means] that one accomplished in right view does not undertake killing and the like, whereas an ordinary person does — this should be understood in detail following the <s>Bahudhātukasūtra</s>.

body.text:
[f. Indriyārtha]
indriyaṃ punar dvāviṃśatividhaṃ /
body.translated_text:
[f. The meaning of <s>indriya</s> (faculty)]
Furthermore, the faculties are twenty-two-fold.

body.text: grahaṇasthānasaṃdhānabhogaśuddhidvayārthataḥ /
body.translated_text: From the meaning of apprehension, abiding, continuity, experience, and the twofold purification.

body.text: grahaṇārthena yāvad viśuddhidvayārthena teṣu tadādhipatyād rūpādiviṣayagrahaṇe hi cakṣurādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇām ādhipatyaṃ sthāne jīvitendriyasya tadādhipatyenāmaraṇāt / kulasandhāne strīpuruṣendriyayor apatyaprasavādhipatyād upabhoge vedanendriyāṇāṃ kuśalākuśalakarmaphalopabhogāt / laukikaviśuddhau śraddhādīnāṃ / lokottaraviśuddhau anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyādīnāṃ /
body.translated_text: In the sense of apprehension up to the sense of the twofold purification — because of their sovereignty therein: the six [faculties] beginning with the eye have sovereignty in the apprehension of objects such as form and the rest. The life-faculty [has sovereignty] in abiding, because of its sovereignty therein — one does not die. The female and male faculties [have sovereignty] in the continuity of the family-line, because of their sovereignty in the production of offspring. The feeling-faculties [have sovereignty] in experience, because of the experience of the fruits of wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>. The [faculties] beginning with faith [have sovereignty] in worldly purification. The [faculties] beginning with the 'I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown' faculty [have sovereignty] in supramundane purification.

body.text: [g. Adhvārtha]

children.translated_text: Another [category is understood] from the meaning of the usefulness of the effect and the cause, and from [their] non-usefulness. // III.20

body.translated_text: [g. The meaning of <s>adhva</s> (time-period)]

body.text: kim aparam adhvatrayaṃ yathāyogaṃ phalahetūpayogārthenātīto 'dhvā phalahetvanupayogārthenānāgato 'dhvā hetūpayogaphalānupayogārthena pratyutpanno 'dhvā veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the other? The three time-periods, in their respective order: the past time-period is to be understood in the sense of the [completed] usefulness of both effect and cause; the future time-period in the sense of the non-usefulness of both effect and cause; and the present time-period in the sense of the usefulness of the cause but non-usefulness of the effect.

body.text: [h. Catuḥsatyārtha]

children.translated_text: From the meaning of feeling, its basis, its cause, and the approach to the cessation of that and its antidote — another [category] is accepted. // III.21

body.translated_text: [h. The meaning of <s>catuḥsatya</s> (the four truths)]

body.text: kim aparaṃ satyacatuṣṭayaṃ / tatra duḥkhasatyaṃ vedanāsanimittārthena yat kiñcid veditam idam atra duḥkhasyeti kṛtvā vedanānimittaṃ punar vedanāsthānīyā dharmā veditavyāḥ / tannimittapratipattitaḥ samudayasatyaṃ duḥkhasatyanimittaṃ yā pratipattiḥ / tayoḥ śamārthena nirodhasatyaṃ / pratipakṣārthena mārgasatyaṃ /
body.translated_text: What is the other? The fourfold truth. Therein, the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>) is [understood] in the sense of the basis of feeling — whatever is experienced, this is [considered] within suffering, and feeling is the indicator; moreover, <s>dharmas</s> that stand in place of feeling should be understood. The truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>) [is understood] from the approach to its cause — the practice that is the cause of the truth of suffering. The truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) is [understood] in the sense of the cessation of both of those. The truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>) is [understood] in the sense of the antidote.

body.text: [i. Yānatrayārtha]

children.text:
guṇadoṣāvikalpena jñānena parataḥ svayaṃ [/]
niryāṇād aparaṃ jñeyaṃ /
children.translated_text: Another should be known through the knowledge of virtues and faults, with and without conceptualization, and through deliverance by another and by oneself.

body.translated_text: [i. The meaning of <s>yānatraya</s> (the three vehicles)]

body.text: yānatrayaṃ yathāyogaṃ / tatra nirvāṇasaṃsārayor guṇadoṣajñānena parataḥ (/) śrutvā niryāṇārthena śrāvakayānaṃ / tenaiva svayam aśrutvā parato niryāṇārthena pratyekabuddhayānaṃ / avikalpena jñānena svayaṃ niryāṇārthena mahāyānaṃ veditavyaṃ //
body.translated_text: The three vehicles, in their respective order: therein, the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle is [understood] in the sense of deliverance through knowledge of the virtues and faults of <s>nirvāṇa</s> and <s>saṃsāra</s>, having heard from another. The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle is [understood] in the sense of deliverance by oneself through that same [knowledge], without having heard from another. The <s>Mahāyāna</s> is to be understood in the sense of deliverance by oneself through non-conceptual knowledge.

body.text: [j. Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtārtha]

children.text:
saprajñaptisahetukāt /
nimittāt praśamāt sārthāt paścimaṃ samudāhṛtaṃ // III.22
children.translated_text: From [what has] designation and cause, from signs, from quiescence, and from [what has] purpose — the last [pair of categories] is stated. // III.22

body.translated_text: [j. The meaning of <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned) and <s>asaṃskṛta</s> (unconditioned)]

body.text: saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaṃ tatra saprajñaptir nāmakāyādayaḥ hetur bījasaṃgṛhītam ālayavijñānaṃ / nimittaṃ pratiṣṭhādehabhogasaṃgṛhītaṃ / pravṛttivijñānasaṃgṛhītāś ca manaudgrahavikalpaḥ / etat saprajñaptisahetukaṃ nimittaṃ sasaṃprayogaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ veditavyaṃ / tatra mano yan nityaṃ manyanākāraṃ / udgrahaḥ pañcavijñānakāyāḥ vikalpo manovijñānaṃ (/) tasya vikalpakatvād asaṃskṛtaṃ punaḥ praśamaś ca nirodhaḥ / praśamārthaś ca tathatā tatra praśamo nirodho mārgaś ca yaś ca praśamo yena ceti kṛtvā praśamārthaḥ tathatā praśamasyārtha iti kṛtvā tathatāyā mārgālambanatvāt / mārgasya praśamatvan tena praśamanāt /
body.translated_text: The conditioned and the unconditioned: therein, that which has designation is name-groups (<s>nāmakāya</s>) and the rest. The cause is the store-consciousness (<s>ālayavijñāna</s>) included as seed. The sign is what is included as the basis-body and enjoyment. And included in the active consciousness (<s>pravṛttivijñāna</s>) are the mind (<s>manas</s>), grasping (<s>udgraha</s>), and conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>). This — having designation, having a cause, and having a sign, together with its associated [factors] — is to be understood as the conditioned. Therein, the mind (<s>manas</s>) is that which constantly has the aspect of 'I-making' (<s>manyana</s>). Grasping consists of the five sense-consciousness groups. Conceptualization is the mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>), because it conceptualizes. As for the unconditioned: quiescence is cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), and that which has the purpose of quiescence is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — therein, quiescence is cessation and the path, and because [suchness] is the purpose of quiescence, <s>tathatā</s> has the meaning of 'the object of quiescence,' since <s>tathatā</s> is the object-support (<s>ālambana</s>) of the path. The path has the nature of quiescence because it pacifies through that.

body.text: ity etenārthena skandhādiṣu jñānaṃ skandhādikauśalyaṃ veditavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Thus, by this meaning, knowledge of the aggregates and so forth is to be understood as skill (<s>kauśalya</s>) in the aggregates and the rest.

body.text:
[Tattvapiṇḍārtha]
tatvasya piṇḍārthaḥ / samāsato dvividhaṃ tatvaṃ / ādarśatatvaṃ / dṛśyatatvaṃ ca tatrādarśatatvaṃ mūlatatvaṃ tatra śeṣāṇāṃ darśanāt / (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 49]

children.text: ) dṛśyatatvaṃ navavidhaṃ nirabhimānadṛśyatatvaṃ / aviparyāsadṛśyatatvaṃ / śrāvakayānaniryāṇadṛśyatatvaṃ / mahāyānaniryāṇadṛśyatatvaṃ / audārikeṇa paripācanāt / sūkṣmeṇa ca vimocanāt paravādinigrahadṛśyatatvaṃ / dṛṣṭāntasanniśrayeṇa yuktyā nigrahāt / mahāyānābhidyotanadṛśyatatvaṃ / sarvākārajñeyapraveśadṛśyatatvaṃ / avitathatathatābhidyotanadṛśyatatvaṃ / ātmagrāhavastusarvābhisandhipraveśadṛśyatatvaṃ ca // ḥ //
children.translated_text: The seen-reality is ninefold: the seen-reality of non-conceit; the seen-reality of non-inversion; the seen-reality of deliverance through the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle; the seen-reality of deliverance through the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — through gross maturation and through subtle liberation; the seen-reality of defeating opponents — through refutation by reasoning based on examples; the seen-reality of illuminating the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; the seen-reality of entry into the knowable in all aspects; the seen-reality of illuminating unerring <s>tathatā</s>; and the seen-reality of entry into the self-grasping, its object, and all its purposes.

body.translated_text:
[Summary meaning of reality (<s>tattva</s>)]
The summary meaning of reality: In brief, reality is twofold — the reality that is the mirror (<s>ādarśatattva</s>) and the reality that is seen (<s>dṛśyatattva</s>). Therein, the mirror-reality is the root-reality, because the rest are seen therein.

body.text: madhyāntavibhāgaśāstre tatvaparicchedas tṛtīyaḥ // ḥ //
body.translated_text: In the treatise <s>Madhyāntavibhāga</s>, this is the third chapter, the Delimitation of Reality (<s>Tattvapariccheda</s>).

body.text:
[CHAPTER IV. PRATIPAKṢABHĀVANĀVASTHĀPHALAPARICCHEDA]
[1.Pratipaksabhāvanā]
pratipakṣabhāvanā bodhipakṣyabhāvanā sedānīṃ vaktavyā /
body.translated_text:
[CHAPTER IV. THE CHAPTER ON THE STAGES AND FRUITS OF CULTIVATING THE ANTIDOTES (<s>PRATIPAKṢABHĀVANĀVASTHĀPHALAPARICCHEDA</s>)]
[1. Cultivation of the Antidotes (<s>Pratipakṣabhāvanā</s>)]
The cultivation of the antidotes is the cultivation of the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>) — this is now to be explained.

body.text:
[a. Catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni]
tatra tāvad ādau /
body.translated_text:
[a. The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)]
Therein, first:

children.text:
dauṣṭhulyāt tarṣahetutvād vastutvād avimohataḥ /
catuḥsatyāvatārāya smṛtyupasthānabhāvanā // IV.1
children.translated_text:
Because of unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), because of being the cause of craving (<s>tarṣa</s>), because of [being] the object (<s>vastu</s>), and because of non-delusion —
the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness is for the purpose of entering into the four truths. // IV.1

body.text: kāyena hi dauṣṭhulyaṃ prabhāvyate / tatparīkṣayā duḥkhasatyam avatarati / tasya sadauṣṭhulyasaṃskāralakṣaṇatvāt / dauṣṭhulyaṃ hi saṃskāraduḥkhatā / tayā sarvaṃ sāsravaṃ vastv āryā duḥkhataḥ paśyantīti / tṛṣṇāhetur vedanā tatparīkṣayā samudayasatyam avatarati / ātmābhiniveśavastu cittaṃ tatparīkṣayā nirodhasatyam avataraty ātmocchedabhayāpagamāt / dharmaparīkṣayā sāṃkleśikavaiyavadānikadharmāsaṃmohāt / mārgasatyam avataraty ataḥ (/) ādau catuḥsatyāvatārāya smṛtyupasthānabhāvanā vyavasthāpyate /
body.translated_text: For unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) is manifested through the body. By examining that [body], the truth of suffering is entered, because [the body] has the characteristic of formations that are always accompanied by unsuitability. For unsuitability is the suffering inherent in formations (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>). Through that, the Noble Ones (<s>āryas</s>) see all conditioned things as suffering. Feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) is the cause of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>); by examining that, the truth of origination is entered. The mind (<s>citta</s>) is the object of the clinging to self (<s>ātmābhiniveśa</s>); by examining that, the truth of cessation is entered, because the fear of annihilation of the self is removed. By examining <s>dharmas</s>, because of non-confusion regarding <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to defilement and purification, the truth of the path is entered. Therefore, the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness is established first for the purpose of entering into the four truths.

body.text:
[b. Catvāri samyakprahāṇāni]
tataḥ samyakprahāṇabhāvanā yasmāt /
body.translated_text:
[b. The four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>)]
Then the cultivation of the right efforts, because:

children.text:
parijñāte vipakṣe ca pratipakṣe ca sarvathā /
tadapāyāyavīryaṃ hi caturdhā saṃpravartate // IV.2
children.translated_text:
When the opponent and the antidote are fully understood in every way,
energy for the removal of that [opponent] proceeds in four ways. // IV.2

body.text: smṛtyupasthānabhāvanayā vipakṣe pratipakṣe ca sarvaprakāraṃ parijñāte vipakṣāpagamāya pratipakṣopagamāya ca vīryañ caturdhā saṃpravartate / utpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāyeti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: Through the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness, when the opponent and the antidote are fully understood in every way, energy proceeds in four ways for the removal of the opponent and for the cultivation of the antidote — 'for the abandonment of arisen evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>' and so forth in detail.

body.text: [c. Catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ]

children.text:
karmaṇyatā sthites tatra sarvārthānāṃ samṛddhaye /
pañcadoṣaprahāṇāṣṭasaṃskārāsevanānvayā // IV.3
children.translated_text: Serviceability of stability therein, for the accomplishment of all purposes, following upon the cultivation of eight formative factors for the abandonment of five faults. [IV.3]

body.translated_text: [c. The Four Bases of Supernatural Power (<s>catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ</s>)]

body.text: tasyāṃ tadapāyāyavīryabhāvanāyāṃ cittasthiteḥ (/) karmaṇyatā catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ sarvārthasamṛddhihetutvāt sthitir atra cittasthitiḥ samādhir veditavyaḥ / ataḥ samyakprahāṇānantaram ṛddhipādāḥ / sā punaḥ karmaṇyatā pañcadoṣaprahāṇāyāṣṭaprahāṇasaṃskārabhāvanānvayā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: In that very cultivation of the antidote through vigor, the serviceability of mental stability (<s>cittasthiti</s>) constitutes the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipādas</s>), because stability is the cause of accomplishing all purposes. 'Stability' here should be understood as mental stability, i.e., <s>samādhi</s>. Therefore, the bases of supernatural power come after the right efforts. That serviceability, moreover, should be understood as following upon the cultivation of eight formative factors (<s>prahāṇasaṃskāras</s>) for the abandonment of five faults.

body.text:
[Paṃca dosāḥ]
katame pañca doṣā ity āha /
body.translated_text:
[The Five Faults]
What are the five faults? He says:

children.text:
kausīdyam avavādasya saṃmoṣo laya uddhataḥ /
asaṃskāro 'tha saṃskāraḥ pañca doṣā ime matāḥ // IV.4
children.translated_text: Laziness, forgetting the instruction, sinking and agitation, non-application, and [over-]application — these are considered the five faults. [IV.4]

body.text: tatra layauddhatyam eko doṣaḥ kriyate / anabhisaṃskāro layauddhatyapraśamanakāle doṣaḥ / abhisaṃskāraḥ praśāntau [/]
body.translated_text: Therein, sinking and agitation are counted as one fault. Non-application at the time of pacifying sinking and agitation is a fault. Application when [they are already] pacified [is a fault].

body.text:
[Aṣṭa prahāṇasaṃskārāḥ]
eṣāṃ prahāṇāya katham aṣṭau prahāṇasaṃskārā vyavasthāpyante / catvāraḥ kausīdyaprahāṇāya cchandavyāyāmaśraddhāprasrabdhayas te punar yathākramaṃ veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text:
[The Eight Formative Factors]
How are eight formative factors established for the abandonment of these? Four are for the abandonment of laziness: desire (<s>chanda</s>), exertion (<s>vyāyāma</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), and pliancy (<s>prasrabdhi</s>). These, moreover, should be understood in order:

body.text: āśrayo 'thāśritas tasya nimittaṃ phalam eva ca /
body.translated_text: The basis, then what is based on it, the cause of that, and the fruit indeed.

body.text: āśrayaś chando vyāyāmasya / āśrito vyāyāmas tasyāśrayasya cchandasya nimittaṃ śraddhā saṃpratyaye (/) saty abhilāṣāt tasyāśritasya vyāyāmasya phalaṃ prasrabdhir ārabdhavīryasya samādhiviśeṣādhigamāc (

children.translated_text: [<s>Mvbh</s> 52]

children.text: ) cheṣāś catvāraḥ prahāṇasaṃskārāḥ smṛtisaṃprajanyacetanopekṣāś caturṇāṃ doṣāṇāṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ pratipakṣās te punaḥ smṛtyādayo veditavyā yathākramaṃ /
children.translated_text: The remaining four formative factors are mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>), volition (<s>cetanā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) — antidotes to the [remaining] four faults respectively. These, moreover — mindfulness and the rest — should be understood in order:

body.translated_text: The basis is desire (<s>chanda</s>). What is based on it is exertion (<s>vyāyāma</s>). The cause of that basis — desire — is faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), because aspiration arises from conviction. The fruit of that which is based on it — exertion — is pliancy (<s>prasrabdhi</s>), from the attainment of special <s>samādhi</s> when vigor has been engaged.

children.text:
ālambane 'saṃmoṣo layauddhatyānubuddhyanā /
tadapāyābhisaṃskāraḥ śāntau praśaṭhavāhitā // IV.5
children.translated_text: Non-forgetfulness regarding the object, awareness of sinking and agitation, application for removing them, and effortless engagement when [they are] pacified. [IV.5]

body.text: smṛtir ālambane 'saṃpramoṣaḥ saṃprajanyaṃ smṛtyasaṃpramoṣe sati layauddhatyānubodhaḥ / anubudhya tadapagamāyābhisaṃskāraś cetanā / tasya layauddhatyasyopaśāntau satyāṃ praśaṭhavāhitā cittasyopekṣā [/]
body.translated_text: Mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) is non-forgetfulness regarding the object. Clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>), when mindfulness is not forgotten, is the awareness of sinking and agitation. Having become aware, the application for their removal is volition (<s>cetanā</s>). When that sinking and agitation have been pacified, the effortless engagement of the mind is equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>).

body.text:
[d. Pañcendriyāṇi]
ṛddhipādānām anantaraṃ pañcendriyāṇi śraddhādīni teṣāṃ kathaṃ vyavasthānaṃ /
body.translated_text:
[d. The Five Faculties (<s>pañcendriyāṇi</s>)]
After the bases of supernatural power come the five faculties beginning with faith. How are they established?

children.text:
ropite mokṣabhāgīye cchandayogādhipatyataḥ /
ālambane 'saṃmoṣāvisāravicayasya ca // IV.6
children.translated_text: When the wholesome root conducive to liberation is planted, through the predominance of desire, application, non-forgetfulness regarding the object, non-distraction, and investigation — [IV.6]

body.text: ādhipatyata iti vartate / ṛddhipādaiḥ karmaṇyacittasyāropite mokṣabhāgīye kuśalamūle cchandādhipatyataḥ prayogādhipatyataḥ / ālambanāsaṃpramoṣādhipatyataḥ / avisārādhipatyataḥ / pravicayādhipatyataś ca / yathākramaṃ pañca śraddhādīnīndriyāṇi veditavyāni /
body.translated_text: 'Through predominance' applies throughout. When, through the bases of supernatural power, the mind has become serviceable and the wholesome root conducive to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya kuśalamūla</s>) has been planted — through the predominance of desire, through the predominance of application, through the predominance of non-forgetfulness of the object, through the predominance of non-distraction, and through the predominance of investigation — the five faculties beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) should be understood respectively.

body.text:
[e. Pañca balāni]
tāny eva śraddhādīni balavanti balānīty ucyante / teṣāṃ punar balavatvaṃ
body.translated_text:
[e. The Five Powers (<s>pañca balāni</s>)]
Those very [faculties] beginning with faith, being strong, are called powers (<s>balāni</s>). Their strength, moreover, [comes from]:

body.text: vipakṣasya hi saṃlekhad /
body.translated_text: Because of the attrition of the adversary.

body.text: yadā tāny aśraddhādibhir vipakṣair na vyavakīryante / kasmāc chraddhādīnāṃ pūrvottaranirdeśaḥ / yasmāt
body.translated_text: When those [faculties] are not scattered by their adversaries such as faithlessness and the rest. Why are faith and the rest taught in a prior and later [set]? Because:

body.text: pūrvasya phalam uttaraṃ /
body.translated_text: The later is the fruit of the prior.

body.text: śraddadhāno hi hetuphalaṃ vīryam ārabhate / ārabdhavīryasya smṛtir upatiṣṭhate / upasthitasmṛteś cittaṃ samādhīyate / samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / avaropitamokṣabhāgīyasyendriyāṇy uktāny atha nirvedhabhāgīyāni kim indriyāvasthāyāṃ veditavyāny āhosvid balāvasthāyāṃ /
body.translated_text: For one who has faith exerts energy as the fruit of [that faith as] cause. For one whose energy is engaged, mindfulness arises. For one whose mindfulness is established, the mind becomes concentrated (<s>samādhīyate</s>). One whose mind is concentrated knows things as they truly are. Having stated the faculties for one whose wholesome root conducive to liberation is planted — now, should the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) be understood at the faculty stage or at the power stage?

children.text: dvau dvau nirvedhabhāgīyāv indriyāṇi balāni ca // IV.7
children.translated_text: The two pairs of aids to penetration [correspond to] the faculties and powers respectively. [IV.7]

body.text: uṣmagataṃ mūrdhānaś cendriyāṇi / kṣāntayo laukikāś cāgradharmā balāni /
body.translated_text: Heat (<s>uṣmagata</s>) and summit (<s>mūrdhānas</s>) [correspond to] the faculties. Patience (<s>kṣāntis</s>) and the supreme mundane <s>dharmas</s> (<s>laukikāś cāgradharmāḥ</s>) [correspond to] the powers.

body.text:
[f. Sapta bodhyaṅgāni]
balānantaraṃ bodhyaṅgāni teṣāṃ kathaṃ vyavasthānaṃ /
body.translated_text:
[f. The Seven Factors of Awakening (<s>sapta bodhyaṅgāni</s>)]
After the powers come the factors of awakening. How are they established?

children.text:
āśrayāṅgaṃ svabhāvāṅgaṃ niryāṇāṅgaṃ tṛtīyakaṃ /
caturtham anuśaṃsāṅgan niḥkleśāṅgaṃ tridhā mataṃ // IV.8
children.translated_text: The basis-factor, the essential-nature-factor, the emergence-factor as the third, the benefit-factor as the fourth, and the non-defilement factor, held to be threefold. [IV.8]

body.text: darśanamārge bodhāv aṅgāni bodhyaṅgāni / tatra bodher āśrayāṅgaṃ smṛtiḥ / svabhāvāṅgaṃ dharmavicayaḥ / niryāṇāṅgaṃ vīryaṃ / anuśansāṅgaṃ prītiḥ / asaṃkleśāṅgaṃ tridhā prasrabdhisamādhyupekṣāḥ / kimarthaṃ punar asaṃkleśāṅgaṃ tridhā deśitaṃ
body.translated_text: On the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>), the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgāni</s>) are the factors of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). Therein, the basis-factor of awakening is mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>). The essential-nature-factor is investigation of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmavicaya</s>). The emergence-factor is energy (<s>vīrya</s>). The benefit-factor is joy (<s>prīti</s>). The non-defilement factor is threefold: pliancy (<s>prasrabdhi</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). For what purpose, then, is the non-defilement factor taught as threefold?

body.text: nidānenāśrayeṇeha svabhāvena ca deśitaṃ /
body.translated_text: It is taught here as cause, basis, and essential nature.

body.text: asaṃkleśasya nidānaṃ prasrabdhir dauṣṭhulyahetutvāt saṃkleśasya / tasyāś ca tatpratipakṣatvād āśrayaḥ samādhiḥ / svabhāvaupekṣā [/]
body.translated_text: Pliancy (<s>prasrabdhi</s>) is the cause of non-defilement, because heaviness (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) is the cause of defilement, and [pliancy] is its antidote. <s>Samādhi</s> is the basis of that [non-defilement]. Equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) is the essential nature [of non-defilement].

body.text:
[g. Aṣṭa mārgāṅgāni]
bodhyaṅgānantaraṃ mārgāṅgāni teṣāṃ kathaṃ vyavasthānaṃ /
body.translated_text:
[g. The Eightfold Path (<s>aṣṭa mārgāṅgāni</s>)]
After the factors of awakening come the path-factors. How are they established?

children.text:
paricchedo 'tha saṃprāptiḥ parasaṃbhāvanā tridhā [//] IV.9
vipakṣapratipakṣaś ca mārgasyāṅgaṃ tad aṣṭadhā /
children.translated_text: Discernment, then accomplishment, engendering confidence in others threefold, [IV.9] and the antidote to the adversary — these are the eightfold factors of the path.

body.text: bhāvanāmārge 'sya paricchedāṅgaṃ samyagdṛṣṭir laukikī lokottarapṛṣṭhalabdhā yayā svādhigamaṃ paricchinatti / parasaṃprāpaṇāṅgaṃ samyaksaṃkalpaḥ samyagvāk ca / sasamutthānayā vācā tatprāpaṇāt / parasaṃbhāvanāṅgaṃ tridhā samyagvākkarmāntājīvās tair hi yathākramaṃ /
body.translated_text: On the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>): the factor of discernment is right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) — mundane, obtained subsequent to the supramundane — by which one discerns one's own attainment. The factor of making others attain is right intention (<s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s>) and right speech (<s>samyagvāc</s>) — because through speech together with its motivation, one makes others attain. The factor of engendering confidence in others is threefold: right speech, right action (<s>samyakkarmānta</s>), and right livelihood (<s>samyagājīva</s>). For through these, respectively:

children.text: dṛṣṭau śīle 'tha saṃlekhe paravijñaptir iṣyate // IV.10
children.translated_text: In [correct] view, in morality, and in asceticism, the informing of others is accepted. [IV.10]

body.text: tasya samyagvācā kathāsāṃkathyaviniścayena prajñāyāṃ saṃbhāvanā bhavati / samyakkarmāntena śīle 'kṛtyākaraṇāt samyagājīvena saṃlekhe dharmeṇa mātrayā ca cīvarādyanveṣaṇāt / vipakṣapratipakṣāṅgaṃ tridhaiva samyagvyāyamasmṛtisamādhayaḥ / eṣāṃ hi yathākramaṃ /
body.translated_text: Through right speech — by the ascertainment of discourse and dialogue — confidence in [correct] view (<s>prajñā</s>) is engendered. Through right action — confidence in morality, by not committing wrong actions. Through right livelihood — confidence in asceticism, by seeking robes and the rest in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> and with moderation. The factor that is the antidote to the adversary is likewise threefold: right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>), right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>), and right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>). For these, in order, are:

body.text: kleśopakleśavaibhutvavipakṣapratipakṣatā /
body.translated_text: The antidote to the adversary of afflictions, secondary afflictions, and [obstruction to] mastery.

body.text: trividho hi vipakṣaḥ kleśo bhāvanāheyaḥ / upakleśo layauddhatyaṃ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Mvbh</s> 55]

children.text: ) vibhutvavipakṣaś ca vaiśeṣikaguṇābhinirhāravibandhaḥ tatra prathamasya samyagvyāyāmaḥ pratipakṣas tena mārgabhāvanāt / dvitīyasya samyaksmṛtiḥ śamathādinimitteṣu sūpasthitasmṛteḥ layauddhatyābhāvāt / tṛtīyasya samyaksamādhiḥ dhyānasanniśrayeṇābhijñādiguṇābhinirhārāt /
children.translated_text: and the adversary of mastery (<s>vaibhutva</s>), which is the obstruction to the production of special qualities. Of these, the antidote to the first is right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>), because through it the path is cultivated. The antidote to the second is right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>), because when mindfulness is well-established with respect to objects of <s>śamatha</s> and the rest, sinking and agitation do not arise. The antidote to the third is right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>), because through the support of <s>dhyāna</s>, special qualities such as the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) are produced.

body.translated_text: The adversary is threefold: afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) to be abandoned by cultivation; secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>), namely sinking and agitation;

body.text:
[h. Pratipakṣabhāvanāprabheda]
saiṣā pratipakṣabhāvanā samāsena trividhā veditavyā /
body.translated_text:
[h. Classification of the Cultivation of the Antidote]
This cultivation of the antidote should be understood, in summary, as threefold:

children.translated_text: Favorable and inverted, with continuation and the reverse — [IV.11]
and cultivation that is un-inverted, free from inversion, and without continuation.

body.text: viparyastāpi aviparyāsānukūlāviparyastā viparyāsānubandhā aviparyastā viparyāsaniranubandhā ca yathākramaṃ pṛthagjanaśaikṣāśaikṣāvasthāsu / bodhisatvānān tv
body.translated_text: [Cultivation that is] inverted yet favorable to the un-inverted, inverted and with continuation of inversion, and un-inverted and without continuation of inversion — these correspond respectively to the stages of the ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), and the adept (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). For <s>bodhisattvas</s>, however:

children.translated_text: Their distinction arises from the object, mental engagement, and attainment. [IV.12]

body.text: śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ hi svāsantānikāḥ kāyādayaḥ ālambanam / bodhisatvānāṃ svaparasāntānikāḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhā anityādibhir ākāraiḥ kāyādīn manasikurvanti / bodhisatvās tv anupalambhayogena / śrāvakapratyekabuddhāḥ smṛtyupasthānādīni bhāvayanti yāvad eva kāyādīnāṃ visaṃyogāya / bodhisatvā na visaṃyogāya / nāvisaṃyogāya / yāvad evāpratiṣṭhitanirvāṇāya / uktā pratipakṣabhāvanā /
body.translated_text: For <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, the objects are the body and the rest in their own continua. For <s>bodhisattvas</s>, [the objects are] those in both their own and others' continua. <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> mentally engage with the body and the rest through aspects of impermanence and the like. <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, however, [engage] through the method of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>). <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> cultivate the foundations of mindfulness and the rest only for the purpose of disengagement from the body and the rest. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> [cultivate them] neither for disengagement nor for non-disengagement, but only for the sake of <s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s> (non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s>). The cultivation of the antidote has been explained.

body.text:
[2. Tatrāvasthā]
tatrāvasthā katamā /
body.translated_text:
[2. Stages Therein (<s>tatrāvasthā</s>)]
What are the stages therein?

children.text:
hetvavasthāvatārākhyā prayogaphalasaṃjñitā /
kāryākāryaviśiṣṭā ca / uttarānuttarā ca sā // IV.13
adhimuktau praveśe ca niryāṇe vyākṛtāv api /
children.translated_text: In [the stage of] conviction, in entering, in emergence, in [receiving] prediction,
in teaching, in consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), in attainment, and in the benefit — [IV.14]
The implementation of the task is indicated.

The stage of the cause, the stage called 'entering,' the stage designated 'application,' the stage of the fruit, and the stage distinguished by what is to be done and what is not to be done, and the lower and the unsurpassed — [IV.13]

body.text: tatra hetvavasthā yā gotrasthasya pudgalasyāvatārāvasthā utpāditabodhicittasya prayogāvasthā cittotpādād ūrdham aprāpte phale / phalāvasthā prāpte / sakaraṇīyāvasthā śaikṣasya / akaraṇīyāvasthā aśaikṣasya / viśeṣāvasthābhijñādiguṇaviśeṣasamanvāgatasya / uttarāvasthā śrāvakādibhyo bhūmipraviṣṭasya bodhisatvasya / anuttarāvasthā buddhasya tata ūrdham avasthābhāvād adhimuktyavasthā bodhisatvānāṃ sarvasyām adhimukticaryābhūmau / praveśāvasthā prathamāyāṃ bhūmau niryāṇāvasthā taduttarāsu ṣaṭsu bhūmiṣu / vyākaraṇāvasthā aṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau kathikatvāvasthā navamyām abhiṣekāvasthā daśamyāṃ / prāptyavasthā buddhānān dharmakāyaḥ / anuśansāvasthā sāṃbhogikaḥ kāyaḥ / kṛtyānuṣṭhānāvasthā nirmāṇakāyaḥ / sarvāpy eṣā bahuvidhāvasthābhisamasya veditavyā /
body.translated_text: Therein, the causal stage is that of a person established in the lineage (<s>gotra</s>); the entry stage is that of one who has generated the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>); the practice stage is from the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> onward until the fruit is not yet attained; the fruit stage is when [the fruit] is attained; the stage of work-to-be-done is the learner's (<s>śaikṣa</s>); the stage of nothing-more-to-be-done is the non-learner's (<s>aśaikṣa</s>); the distinctive stage is of one endowed with distinctive qualities such as <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge); the higher stage is of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has entered the stages, [being higher] than <s>śrāvakas</s> and the rest; the unsurpassed stage is the <s>Buddha</s>'s, there being no further stage beyond that. The stage of aspiration is the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' entire aspiration-conduct stage (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>); the stage of entry is at the first stage; the stage of progress is at the next six stages; the stage of prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) is at the eighth stage; the stage of exposition is at the ninth; the stage of consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) is at the tenth. The stage of attainment of the <s>Buddhas</s> is the <s>dharmakāya</s>; the stage of benefit is the enjoyment body (<s>sāṃbhogika kāya</s>); the stage of activity-performance is the emanation body (<s>nirmāṇakāya</s>). All of this manifold [classification of] stages should be understood as comprehensive.

children.text:
dharmadhātau tridhā puuaḥ /
aśuddhāśuddhaśuddhā ca viśuddhā ca yathārhataḥ // IV.15
children.translated_text: In the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, [there are] three [states]: the impure, the impure-and-pure, and the pure, as appropriate. // IV.15

body.text: tatrāśuddhāvasthā hetvavasthām upādāya yāvat prayogād aśuddhaśuddhāvasthā (

children.translated_text: <s>Mvbh</s> 57
is of the learners (<s>śaikṣas</s>); the pure state is of the non-learners (<s>aśaikṣas</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, the impure state is from the causal stage up to [the end of] the practice [stage]; the impure-and-pure state

body.text: pudgalānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ yathāyogam ato matam /
body.translated_text: The classification of persons is held [to be established] from this, as appropriate.

body.text: ato 'vasthāprabhedād yathāyogaṃ pudgalānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ (/) veditavyam ayaṃ gotrastho 'yam avatīrṇa ity evamādi / uktāvasthā [/]
body.translated_text: From this differentiation of stages, the classification of persons is to be understood as appropriate — 'this one is established in the lineage,' 'this one has entered,' and so forth. The stages have been stated.

body.text:
[3. Phalaprāpti]
phalaprāptiḥ katamā /
body.translated_text: [3. Attainment of Fruits] What is the attainment of fruits?

children.translated_text: Receptivity, called 'maturation' (<s>vipāka</s>); power, due to the predominance of that; // IV.16

children.text: rucir vṛddhir viśuddhiś ca phalam etad yathākramaṃ /
children.translated_text: Inclination, growth, and purification — this is the fruit, in order.

body.text: bhājanatvaṃ yaḥ kuśalānukūlo vipākaḥ / balaṃ yā bhājanatvādhipatyāt kuśalasyādhimātratā / rucir yā pūrvābhyāsāt kuśalaruciḥ / vṛddhir yā pratyutpanne kuśaladharmābhyāsāt kuśalamūlaparipuṣṭiḥ / viśuddhir yad āvaraṇaprahāṇaṃ / etad yathākramaṃ phalaṃ pañcavidhaṃ veditavyam / vipākaphalam adhipatiphalan niṣyandaphalaṃ puruṣakāraphalaṃ visaṃyogaphalañ ca /
body.translated_text: Receptivity (<s>bhājanatva</s>) is that maturation which is favorable to virtue. Power (<s>bala</s>) is the intensity of virtue due to the predominance of receptivity. Inclination (<s>ruci</s>) is the taste for virtue from previous practice. Growth (<s>vṛddhi</s>) is the nourishment of the roots of virtue from the practice of virtuous <s>dharmas</s> in the present. Purification (<s>viśuddhi</s>) is the abandonment of obscurations. This fivefold fruit is to be understood in order: maturation-fruit, predominance-fruit, outflow-fruit, effort-fruit, and separation-fruit.

children.text: uttarottaram ādyañ ca tadabhyāsāt samāptitaḥ // IV.17
children.translated_text: Each [stage] is [the fruit] of the preceding one, and [also] the initial [fruit]; from practice and from completion — // IV.17

children.text:
ānukūlyād vipakṣāc ca visaṃyogād viśeṣataḥ /
uttarānuttaratvāc ca phalam anyat samāsataḥ // IV.18
children.translated_text: from favorability, from opposition, from separation, from distinction, and from being higher and unsurpassed — the remaining fruits [are to be understood] in brief. // IV.18

body.text: uttarottaraphalaṃ gotrāc cittotpāda ity evamādi paraṃparayā veditavyaṃ / ādiphalaṃ prathamato lokottaradharmapratilambhaḥ / abhyāsaphalaṃ tasmāt pareṇa śaikṣāvasthāyāṃ / samāptiphalam aśaikṣādharmāḥ / ānukūlyaphalam upaniṣadbhāvenottarottaraphalam eva veditavyaṃ / vipakṣaphalaṃ prahāṇamārgo yad evādiphalaṃ / pratipakṣo 'bhipretaḥ / visaṃyogaphalaṃ nirodhasākṣātkriyā abhyāsaphalaṃ samāptiphalaṃ ca kleśavisaṃyogaḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Mvbh</s> 58

children.text: ) śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāṃ yathākramaṃ / viśeṣaphalam abhijñādiko guṇaviśeṣaḥ / uttaraphalaṃ bodhisatvabhūmayas tadanyayānottaratvād anuttaraphalaṃ buddhabhūmiḥ / etāni catvāri abhyāsasamāptiphalaprabheda eva etad anyat phalaṃ samāsanirdeśato vyāsatas tv aparimāṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: of the learners and non-learners respectively. The distinction-fruit is the distinctive qualities such as <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge). The higher fruit consists of the <s>bodhisattva</s> stages, being higher than the other vehicles. The unsurpassed fruit is the <s>Buddha</s>-stage. These last four are subdivisions of the practice-fruit and the completion-fruit. This remaining fruit is indicated in brief; in detail, it is immeasurable.

body.translated_text: The fruit of each successive [stage] is to be understood as arising sequentially from the lineage, the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, and so forth. The initial fruit is the first attainment of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>. The practice-fruit is thereafter, in the learner's stage. The completion-fruit consists of the non-learner's <s>dharmas</s>. The favorability-fruit is to be understood as the successive fruit itself, through being a condition. The opposition-fruit is the path of abandonment, which is the initial fruit itself — the antidote is intended. The separation-fruit is the direct realization of cessation; the practice-fruit and completion-fruit are the separation from afflictions

body.text:
[Pratipakṣabhāvanāpiṇḍārtha]
tatra pratipakṣabhāvanāyāḥ piṇḍārthaḥ / vyutpattibhāvanā nirlekhabhāvanā parikarmabhāvanā / uttarasamārambhabhāvanā / śliṣṭabhāvanā darśanamārgaśleṣāt / praviṣṭabhāvanā utkṛṣṭabhāvanā ādibhāvanā madhyabhāvanā paryavasānabhāvanā / sottarā bhāvanā niruttarā ca bhāvanā yālambanamanaskāraprāptiviśiṣṭā // avasthānāṃ piṇḍārthaḥ / bhavyatāvasthā gotrasthasya / ārambhāvasthā yāvat prayogāt / asuddhāvasthā aśuddhaśuddhāvasthā viśuddhāvasthā / sālaṃkārāvasthā / vyāptyavasthā daśabhūmivyāpanāt / anuttarāvasthā ca // phalānāṃ piṇḍārthaḥ saṃgrahataḥ tadviśeṣataḥ pūrvābhyāsataḥn uttarottaranirhārataḥ / uddeśato nirdeśataś ca / tatra saṃgrahataḥ / pañca phalāni / tadviśeṣataḥ śeṣāṇi / pūrvābhyāsataḥ vipākaphalaṃ / uttarottaranirhāratas tadanyāni catvāri / uddeśataḥ uttarottaraphalādīni catvāri nirdeśataḥ ānukūlyaphalādini ṣaṭ / teṣām eva (

children.translated_text: <s>Mvbh</s> 59
— from the explanation of those very four. //

body.translated_text: [Condensed Meaning of the Cultivation of the Antidote] Therein, the condensed meaning of the cultivation of the antidote: the cultivation of understanding; the cultivation of outline; the cultivation of preparation; the cultivation of undertaking the higher; the joined cultivation — from joining with the path of seeing; the entered cultivation; the elevated cultivation; the initial cultivation; the middle cultivation; the final cultivation; cultivation with something higher; cultivation without anything higher — which are distinguished by object, mental engagement, attainment, and distinction. // The condensed meaning of the stages: the stage of fitness is of one in the lineage; the stage of undertaking is up to the practice-[stage]; the impure stage; the impure-and-pure stage; the pure stage; the adorned stage; the pervading stage — from pervading the ten stages; and the unsurpassed stage. // The condensed meaning of the fruits: by inclusion, by their distinctions, by previous practice, by successive realization. By indication and by explanation. Therein, by inclusion: five fruits. By their distinctions: the remaining [fruits]. By previous practice: the maturation-fruit. By successive realization: the other four. By indication: the four beginning with the successive fruit. By explanation: the six beginning with the favorability-fruit.

body.text: madhyāntavibhāge pratipakṣabhāvanāvasthāphalaparicchedaś caturthaḥ // ḥ
body.translated_text: In the <s>Madhyāntavibhāga</s>, the fourth chapter: the chapter on the cultivation of the antidote, stages, and fruits. //

body.text:
[CHAPTER V. YĀNĀNUTTARYAPARICCHEDA]
[1. Trividhānuttarya]
yānānuttaryam idānīṃ vaktavyaṃ / tad ucyate /
body.translated_text: [CHAPTER V. CHAPTER ON THE UNSURPASSED VEHICLE (<s>YĀNĀNUTTARYAPARICCHEDA</s>)] [1. The Threefold Unsurpassed] Now the unsurpassed nature of the vehicle is to be stated. It is said:

children.text:
ānuttaryaṃ prapattau hi punar ālambane mataṃ /
samudāgama uddiṣṭaṃ /
children.translated_text: The unsurpassed is held [to be] in the practice, again in the object, and is indicated in the attainment.

body.text: trividham ānuttaryaṃ mahāyāne yenaitad anuttaraṃ yānaṃ pratipattyānuttaryaṃ / ālambanānuttaryaṃ / samudāgamānuttaryañ ca /
body.translated_text: The unsurpassed is threefold in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, by which this is the unsurpassed vehicle: the unsurpassed of practice, the unsurpassed of object, and the unsurpassed of attainment.

body.text:
[2. Pratipattyānuttarya]
tatra pratipattyānuttaryaṃ daśapāramitāpratipattito veditavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: [2. Unsurpassed of Practice] Therein, the unsurpassed of practice is to be understood through the practice of the ten <s>pāramitās</s>.

children.translated_text: The practice is sixfold. // V.1

body.text: tāsu pāramitāsu /
body.translated_text: In those <s>pāramitās</s>:

children.text:
paramātha manaskāre anudharme 'ntavarjane /
viśiṣṭā cāviśiṣṭā ca /
children.translated_text: The supreme, in mental engagement, in accordance with <s>Dharma</s>, avoiding the two extremes, the distinguished, and the undistinguished.

body.text: ity eṣā ṣaḍvidhā pratipattir yad uta paramā pratipattiḥ / manaskārapratipattir anudharmapratipattiḥ / antadvayavarjitā pratipattiḥ viśistā pratipattiḥ / aviśiṣṭā ca pratipattiḥ /
body.translated_text: This is the sixfold practice: the supreme practice, the practice of mental engagement, the practice in accordance with <s>Dharma</s>, the practice avoiding the two extremes, the distinguished practice, and the undistinguished practice.

body.text:
[a. Paramā pratipattiḥ]
tatra /
body.translated_text: [a. Supreme Practice] Therein:

children.translated_text: The supreme is twelvefold. // V.2
Greatness, extensiveness, predominant purpose, inexhaustibility,

children.text: nairantaryam akṛcchratvaṃ vittatvaṃ ca parigrahaḥ // V.3
children.translated_text: continuity, effortlessness, skillfulness, and commitment, // V.3
undertaking, attainment, outflow, and completion — [these] are held to be supreme.

body.text: ity eṣā dvādaśavidhā paramā matā / yad utaudāryaparamatā āyatatvaparamatā adhikāraparamatā akṣayatvaparamatā nairantaryaparamatā akṛcchratvaparamatā / vittatvaparamatā parigrahaparamatā / ārambhaparamatā pratilambhaparamatā niṣyandaparamatā niṣpattiparamatā ca / tatraudāryaparamatā sarvalaukikasaṃpattyanarthitvenotkṛṣṭatayā ca veditavyā / āyatatvaparamatā trikalpāsaṃkhyeyaparibhāvanāt / adhikāraparamatā sarvasatvārthakriyādhikārāt / akṣayatvaparamatā mahābodhipariṇāmanayātyantam aparyādānān nairantaryaparamatātmaparasamatādhimokṣāt sarvasatvadānādibhiḥ pāramitāparipūraṇād akṛcchratvaparamatānumodanāmātreṇa paradānādīnāṃparamitāparipūraṇāt / vittatvaparamatā / gaganagañjasamādhyādibhir dānādiparipūraṇāt parigrahaparamatā nirvikalpajñānaparigṛhītatvāt / ārambhaparamatādhimukticaryābhūmāv adhimātrāyāṃ kṣāntau pratilambhaparamatā prathamāyāṃ bhūmau / niṣyandaparamatā / tadanyāsv aṣṭāsu bhūmiṣu / niṣpattiparamatā daśamyāṃ bhūmau tathāgatyāṃ ca / bodhisatvaniṣpattyā buddhaniṣpattyā ca /
body.translated_text: This twelvefold [practice] is held to be supreme: the supremacy of greatness, extensiveness, predominant purpose, inexhaustibility, continuity, effortlessness, skillfulness, commitment, undertaking, attainment, outflow, and completion. Therein, the supremacy of greatness is to be understood as not desiring all worldly prosperity and as being superior. The supremacy of extensiveness is from cultivating [the practice] over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s>. The supremacy of predominant purpose is from undertaking the welfare of all sentient beings. The supremacy of inexhaustibility is from the utter non-depletion [of merit] through dedication to great awakening. The supremacy of continuity is from fulfilling the <s>pāramitās</s> through generosity and the rest toward all beings, based on the conviction of the equality of self and others. The supremacy of effortlessness is from fulfilling the <s>pāramitās</s> merely through rejoicing in the generosity and the rest of others. The supremacy of skillfulness is from fulfilling generosity and the rest through <s>samādhis</s> such as the '<s>Gaganagañja</s>-<s>samādhi</s>.' The supremacy of commitment is from being embraced by non-conceptual knowledge. The supremacy of undertaking is at the aspiration-conduct stage, in the highest degree of patience. The supremacy of attainment is at the first stage. The supremacy of outflow is at the other eight stages. The supremacy of completion is at the tenth stage and at <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood — from the completion of the <s>bodhisattva</s> and the completion of the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: tataś ca paramārthena daśa pāramitā matāḥ // V.4
children.translated_text: And therefore, in the ultimate sense, the ten <s>pāramitās</s> are held. // V.4

body.text: yata eṣā dvādaśavidhā paramatā etāsu saṃvidyate / tataḥ paramā (

children.translated_text: <s>Mvbh</s> 62

children.text: ) ity anenārthena daśa pāramitāḥ / katamā daśety ekeṣāṃ tannāmavyutpādanārtham ucyate /
children.translated_text: — in this sense [the word] '<s>pāramitā</s>' [is used for] the ten. 'What are the ten?' — for those who wish to know the etymology of that name, it is said:

body.translated_text: Since this twelvefold supremacy is found in them, therefore [they are called] 'supreme' (<s>paramā</s>)

children.text:
dānaṃ śīlaṃ kṣamā vīryaṃ dhyānaṃ prajñā upāyatā /
praṇidhānaṃ balaṃ jñānam etāḥ pāramitā daśeti // V.5
children.translated_text: Generosity (<s>dāna</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣamā</s>), energy (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), power (<s>bala</s>), and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) — these are the ten <s>pāramitās</s>. // V.5

body.text: kim āsāṃ pratyekaṃ karma /
body.translated_text: What is the specific function of each of these?

children.text:
anugraho 'vighātaś ca karma tasya ca marṣaṇaṃ /
guṇavṛddhiś ca sāmarthyam avatāravimocane /
akṣayatvaṃ sadā vṛttir niyataṃ bhogapācane // V.6
children.translated_text: Assistance, non-obstruction, and the function of enduring that; increase of virtues, capability in [causing] entry and liberation; inexhaustibility, constant activity, definiteness in [bringing about] the enjoyment and maturation [of <s>Dharma</s>]. // V.6

body.text: ity etad āsāṃ karma yathākramaṃ / dānena hi bodhisatvaḥ satvān anugṛhṇāti / śīlenopaghātaṃ pareṣāṃ na karoti / kṣāntyā paraiḥ kṛtam upaghātaṃ marṣayati / vīryeṇa guṇān vardhayati / dhyānena rddhyādibhir āvarjyāvatārayati / prajñayā samyagavavādadānād vimocayati / upāyakauśalyapāramitayā mahābodhipariṇāmanād dānādīn akṣayān karoti / praṇidhānapāramitayānukūlopapattiparigrahāt / sarvajanmasu buddhotpādārāgaṇato dānādiṣu sadā pravartate balapāramitayā pratisaṃkhyānabhāvanābalābhyāṃ niyataṃ dānādiṣu pravartate / vipakṣānabhibhavāt / jñānapāramitayā yathārutadharmasaṃmohāpagamād dānādyādhipateyadharmasaṃbhogañ ca pratyanubhavati / satvāṃś ca paripācayati / uktā paramā pratipattiḥ /
body.translated_text: This is the function of these [<s>pāramitās</s>], in order: Through <s>dāna</s> (giving), the <s>bodhisattva</s> benefits beings. Through <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline), he does not cause harm to others. Through <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), he endures harm done by others. Through <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), he increases virtuous qualities. Through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), he attracts and introduces [beings] by means of <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural powers) and so forth. Through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), he liberates [beings] by giving correct instruction. Through the <s>upāyakauśalya-pāramitā</s> (perfection of skillful means), by dedicating [merit] toward great awakening, he makes <s>dāna</s> and the rest inexhaustible. Through the <s>praṇidhāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of vows), by obtaining favorable rebirths, he always engages in <s>dāna</s> and the rest in all lives, attending to the arising of Buddhas. Through the <s>bala-pāramitā</s> (perfection of powers), by the two powers of analytical reflection and meditation, he definitively engages in <s>dāna</s> and the rest, without being overcome by opposing forces. Through the <s>jñāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of knowledge), by the removal of confusion about the <s>Dharma</s> as [merely] literal, he experiences the enjoyment of the <s>Dharma</s> governed by <s>dāna</s> and the rest, and he matures beings. The supreme practice has been explained.

body.text: [b. Manasikārapratipatti]
body.translated_text: [b. Practice of Mental Attention]

body.text: manasikārapratipattiḥ katamā /
body.translated_text: What is the practice of mental attention (<s>manasikāra-pratipatti</s>)?

children.text:
yathāprajñaptito dharmamahāyānamanaskriyā /
bodhisatvasya satataṃ prajñayā triprakārayā // V.7
children.translated_text: Mental attention to the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, as taught, is constant for the <s>bodhisattva</s>, through <s>prajñā</s> of three kinds. // V.7

body.text: dānādīny adhikṛtya yathāprajñaptānāṃ sūtrādidharmāṇāṃ mahāyāne manasikaraṇam abhīkṣṇaṃ śrutacintābhāvanāmayyā prajñayā manasikārapratipattiḥ / sā triprakārayā prajñayā manasikriyā kaṃ guṇaṃkaroti /
body.translated_text: The practice of mental attention (<s>manasikāra-pratipatti</s>) is the continuous mental attention in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> to the <s>Dharma</s> teachings such as <s>sūtras</s>, as they have been taught with respect to <s>dāna</s> and the rest, through <s>prajñā</s> arising from hearing, reflection, and meditation. What benefit does that mental attention, through <s>prajñā</s> of three kinds, produce?

body.text: dhātupuṣṭyai praveśāya cārthasiddhyai bhavaty asau /
body.translated_text: It serves for the nourishment of the [Buddha-]element, for entry [into meaning], and for the accomplishment of the goal.

body.text: śrutamayyā prajñayā manasikurvato dhātupuṣṭir bhavati / cintāmayyā tasya śrutasyārthaṃ bhāvena praviśati / bhāvanāmayyārthasiddhiṃ prāpnoti bhūmipraveśapariśodhanāt /
body.translated_text: For one who applies mental attention through <s>prajñā</s> arising from hearing (<s>śrutamayī</s>), there is nourishment of the [Buddha-]element (<s>dhātu</s>). Through <s>prajñā</s> arising from reflection (<s>cintāmayī</s>), one enters into the meaning of what was heard in its true nature. Through <s>prajñā</s> arising from meditation (<s>bhāvanāmayī</s>), one attains the accomplishment of the goal, through entering and purifying the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>).

children.text: saṃyuktā dharmacaritaiḥ sā jñeyā daśabhiḥ punaḥ // V.8
children.translated_text: It should be known as conjoined with ten practices of the <s>Dharma</s>. // V.8

body.text: sā punar manasikārapratipattiḥ / daśabhir dharmacaritaiḥ parigṛhītā veditavyā katamad daśadhā dharmacaritaṃ /
body.translated_text: That practice of mental attention should be understood as encompassed by ten practices of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmacarita</s>). What are these ten <s>Dharma</s>-practices?

children.text:
lekhanā pūjanā dānaṃ śravaṇaṃ vācanodgrahaḥ /
prakāśanātha svādhyāyaś cintanā bhāvanā ca tat // V.9
children.translated_text: Copying, worshipping, giving, hearing, reciting, memorizing, expounding, and also recitation to oneself, reflection, and meditation — that [is the tenfold practice]. // V.9

body.text: mahāyānasya lekhanaṃ pūjanaṃ parebhyo dānaṃ pareṇa vācyamānasya śravaṇaṃ / svayaṃ ca vācanaṃ / udgrahaṇaṃ / parebhyo deśanaṃ granthasyārthasya vā svādhyāyanaṃ / cintanaṃ bhāvanañ ca /
body.translated_text: Copying the <s>Mahāyāna</s> [texts], worshipping them, giving them to others, hearing when they are recited by others, reciting them oneself, memorizing them, teaching them to others, reciting the text or its meaning to oneself, reflecting [on them], and meditating [on them].

body.text: ameyapuṇyaskandhaṃ hi caritan tad daśātmakaṃ /
body.translated_text: For that tenfold practice is an immeasurable mass of merit.

body.text: kasmān mahāyāna eva dharmacaritam atyarthaṃ mahāphalan deśyate sūtreṣu na punaḥ śrāvakayāne / dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ /
body.translated_text: Why is it taught in the <s>sūtras</s> that <s>Dharma</s>-practice in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> alone is exceedingly great in its fruit, and not in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>? For two reasons:

body.text: viśeṣād akṣayatvāc ca /
body.translated_text: Because of its distinction and because of its inexhaustibility.

body.text: kathaṃ viśeṣāt / katham akṣayatvāt /
body.translated_text: How is it due to distinction? How is it due to inexhaustibility?

children.translated_text: Because of benefiting others and because of non-cessation. // V.10

body.text: parānugrahavṛttitvād viśiṣṭatvaṃ / parinirvāṇe 'py aśamāt / anuparamād akṣayatvaṃ veditavyaṃ / uktā manasikārapratipattiḥ /
body.translated_text: Its distinction is due to its functioning for the benefit of others. Its inexhaustibility should be understood as due to non-cessation, its non-discontinuation even at <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. The practice of mental attention has been explained.

body.text:
[c. Anudharmapratipatti]
anudharmapratipattiḥ katamā /
body.translated_text:
[c. Practice in Conformity with the Dharma]
What is the practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>anudharmapratipatti</s>)?

body.text: avikṣiptāviparyāsapraṇatā cānudhārmikī /
body.translated_text: The practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> is non-distracted and matured without error.

body.text: ity eṣā dvividhānudharmapratipattiḥ / yad utāvikṣiptā cāviparyāsapariṇatā ca /
body.translated_text: This practice in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>anudharmapratipatti</s>) is twofold: namely, non-distracted and matured without error (<s>aviparyāsa</s>).

body.text:
[Avikṣepapariṇatā]
tatra ṣaḍvidhavikṣepābhāvād avikṣiptā / tatra ṣaḍvidho vikṣepaḥ / prakṛtivikṣepaḥ / bahirdhāvikṣepaḥ / adhyātmavikṣepaḥ nimittavikṣepaḥ dauṣṭhulyavikṣepaḥ manasikāravikṣepaś ca / sa eṣa kiṃlakṣaṇo veditavya ity ata āha /
body.translated_text:
[Non-distraction]
In this regard, it is non-distracted due to the absence of six kinds of distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>). There are six kinds of distraction: natural distraction (<s>prakṛti-vikṣepa</s>), external distraction (<s>bahirdhā-vikṣepa</s>), internal distraction (<s>adhyātma-vikṣepa</s>), sign-distraction (<s>nimitta-vikṣepa</s>), affliction-distraction (<s>dauṣṭhulya-vikṣepa</s>), and attention-distraction (<s>manasikāra-vikṣepa</s>). To explain what characterizes each, the text says:

children.translated_text: Arising [from concentration], dispersion toward sense-objects, likewise relishing, sinking and agitation, // V.11
Conception of [gaining] esteem, and ego-making even in mental attention,

children.text: hīnacittaṃca vikṣepaḥ parijñeyo hi dhīmatā // V.12
children.translated_text: And inferior mind — distraction is to be fully known by the wise. // V.12

body.text: ity evaṃlakṣaṇaḥ ṣaḍvidho vikṣepo yo bodhisatvena parijñeyaḥ / tatra vyutthānaṃ samādhitaḥ pañcabhir vijñānakāyaiḥ prakṛtivikṣepaḥ viṣaye visāro bahirdhāvikṣepaḥ / samādher āsvādanā layauddhatyaṃ cādhyātmavikṣepaḥ / saṃbhāvanābhisandhiḥ nimittavikṣepaḥ / tan nimittaṃ kṛtvā prayogāt / sāhaṃkāramanaskāratā dauṣṭhulyavikṣepaḥ / dauṣṭhulyavaśenāsmimānasamudācārāt / hīnacittatvaṃ / manasikāravikṣepaḥ hīnayānamanasikārasamudācārāt /
body.translated_text: Thus characterized, the sixfold distraction is to be fully known by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Here, arising from <s>samādhi</s> through the five sense-consciousness groups is natural distraction (<s>prakṛti-vikṣepa</s>). Dispersion toward sense-objects is external distraction (<s>bahirdhā-vikṣepa</s>). Relishing <s>samādhi</s>, and sinking and agitation, are internal distraction (<s>adhyātma-vikṣepa</s>). Conception of [gaining] esteem is sign-distraction (<s>nimitta-vikṣepa</s>), since one exerts oneself using that as a motive. Mental attention accompanied by ego-making is affliction-distraction (<s>dauṣṭhulya-vikṣepa</s>), since the conceit 'I am' arises under the influence of affliction. Having an inferior mind is attention-distraction (<s>manasikāra-vikṣepa</s>), since the mental attention of the inferior vehicle (<s>Hīnayāna</s>) arises.

body.text:
[Aviparyāsapariṇatā]
tatrāviparyāso daśavidhe vastuni veditavyaḥ / yad uta /
body.translated_text:
[Non-confusion]
In this regard, non-confusion (<s>aviparyāsa</s>) should be understood with respect to ten objects, namely:

children.translated_text: In the mental attention to words and meaning, in non-dispersion, in the two characteristics, in impurity and purity, in adventitious nature, in fearlessness and non-elation, // V.13

body.text: tatra /
body.translated_text: Regarding these:

children.text:
saṃyogāt saṃstavāc caiva viyogād apy asaṃstavāt /
arthasatvam asatvañ ca vyañjane so 'viparyayaḥ /] V.14
children.translated_text: Through combination and through connection, and also through separation and disconnection, the meaningfulness and meaninglessness of words — that is the non-confusion regarding words. // V.14

body.text: saṃyoge sati vyañjanānām avicchinnoccāraṇatayā asya cedaṃ nāmeti saṃstavāt sārthakatvaṃ viparyayān nirarthakatvam iti / yad evandarśanaṃ so 'viparyāso vyañjane veditavyaḥ / katham arthe 'viparyāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: When there is combination, through the uninterrupted pronunciation of words, there is meaningfulness due to the connection 'this is the name of that'; confusion [would mean] meaninglessness. Such seeing is the non-confusion (<s>aviparyāsa</s>) regarding words to be understood. How is there non-confusion regarding meaning?

children.text:
dvayena pratibhāsatvaṃ tathā cāvidyamānatā j
arthe sa cāviparyāsaḥ sadasatvena varjitaḥ // V.15
children.translated_text: The fact of appearing through duality, and likewise its non-existence [as it appears] — the non-confusion regarding meaning is free from both existence and non-existence. // V.15

body.text: dvayena grāhyagrāhakatvena pratibhāsate tadākarotpattitaḥ / tathā (

children.translated_text: Mvbh 66

children.text: ) ca na vidyate / yathā pratibhāsata iti / arthe yad darśanaṃ sa tatrāviparyāsaḥ arthasya satvena varjito grāhyagrāhakābhāvād asatvena varjitaḥ / tatpratibhāsabhrāntisadbhāvāt /
children.translated_text: it does not exist as it appears. Such seeing regarding meaning is the non-confusion there. [This non-confusion] regarding meaning is free from [asserting] existence, since <s>grāhya</s> (the apprehended) and <s>grāhaka</s> (the apprehender) do not exist [as such], and free from [asserting] non-existence, since the confusion that appears as them does in fact exist.

children.text:
tajjalpabhāvito jalpamanaskāras tadāśrayaḥ
manaskāre 'viparyāso dvayaprakhyānakāraṇe // V.16
children.translated_text: Mental attention conditioned by the conceptual proliferation of that [duality], which is the basis of that [proliferation] — non-confusion regarding mental attention is [understanding it as] the cause of the appearance of duality. // V.16

body.translated_text: [Meaning] appears through duality — as apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) and apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>) — since [consciousness] arises in the form of those. And likewise

body.text: grāhyagrāhakajalpaparibhāvito jalpamanaskāras tasya grāhyagrāhakavikalpasyāśrayo bhavatīty ayaṃ manaskāre 'viparyāsaḥ / katamasmin manaskāre grāhyagrāhakasaṃprakhyānakāraṇe sa hy asau jalpamanaskāro 'bhilāpasaṃjñāparibhāvitatvāt grāhyagrāhakavikalpāśrayo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Mental attention conditioned by the conceptual proliferation (<s>jalpa</s>) of <s>grāhya</s> and <s>grāhaka</s> becomes the basis of that conceptual construction of <s>grāhya</s> and <s>grāhaka</s> — this is the non-confusion regarding mental attention. Regarding which mental attention? That which is the cause of the appearance of <s>grāhya</s> and <s>grāhaka</s>. For that mental attention of conceptual proliferation, being conditioned by the notion of verbal designation (<s>abhilāpa-saṃjñā</s>), should be understood as the basis of the conceptual construction of <s>grāhya</s> and <s>grāhaka</s>.

children.text:
māyādivad asatvañ ca satvaṃ cārthasya tan mataṃ [/]
so 'visāre 'viparyāso bhāvābhāvāvisārataḥ // V.17
children.translated_text: Like an illusion and so forth, the non-existence and existence of the object is so regarded; that is the non-confusion regarding non-dispersion, through non-dispersion into [asserting] existence or non-existence. // V.17

body.text: yat tad arthasyāsatvaṃ satvaṃ cānantaram uktaṃ / tan māyādivan mataṃ yathā māyā na hastyādibhāvenāsti na ca naivāsti / tadbhrāntimātrāstitvāt / evam artho 'pi na cāsti yathā saṃprakhyāti grāhyagrāhakatvena na ca naivāsti tadbhrāntimātrāstitvāt / ādiśabdena marīcisvapnodakacandrādayo dṛṣṭāntā yathāyogaṃ veditavyā iti yan māyādyupamārthe darśanād avisāraṃ cetasaḥ paśyati so 'visāre 'viparyāsas tena bhāvābhāvayoś cittasyāvisaraṇāt /
body.translated_text: That non-existence and existence of the object, just stated, is regarded as like an illusion (<s>māyā</s>) and so forth. Just as an illusion does not exist as an elephant and so forth, yet is not entirely non-existent — since the mere confusion of it does exist — so too the object does not exist as it appears, namely as <s>grāhya</s> and <s>grāhaka</s>, yet is not entirely non-existent, since the mere confusion of it does exist. By the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), examples such as a mirage, a dream, [a reflection in] water, [a reflection of] the moon, and so on, should be understood as appropriate. Thus, seeing the object through the simile of illusion and the rest as non-dispersion of the mind — that is the non-confusion regarding non-dispersion, because the mind does not disperse toward [asserting either] existence or non-existence.

children.translated_text: The mere-name-ness of everything, for the non-occurrence of all conceptual construction — [that is] the non-confusion regarding the specific characteristic.

body.text: sarvam idaṃ nāmamātraṃ / yad idaṃ cakṣūrūpaṃ yāvan manodharmā iti yaj jñānaṃ sarvavikalpānāṃ pratipakṣeṇa ayaṃ svalakṣaṇe 'viparyāsaḥ / katamasmin svalakṣaṇe /
body.translated_text: All this is mere name — that which is eye and form, up to mind and <s>dharmas</s> — such knowledge, as the antidote to all conceptual constructions, is the non-confusion regarding the specific characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). Regarding which specific characteristic?

children.translated_text: Regarding the ultimate as the specific characteristic. // V.18

body.text: saṃvṛtyā tu nedaṃ nāmamātram iti gṛhyate /
body.translated_text: But conventionally, it is not apprehended as mere name.

children.text:
dharmadhātuvinirmukto yasmād dharmo na vidyate /
sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ tasmāt sa ca tatrāviparyayaḥ // V.19
children.translated_text: Since no <s>dharma</s> is found apart from the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, that is the general characteristic, and the non-confusion there [is regarding that]. // V.19

body.text: na hi dharmanairātmyena vinā kaścid dharmo vidyate / tasmād dharmadhātuḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sāmānyaṃ lakṣaṇam iti / yad evaṃjñānam ayaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇe 'viparyāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: For apart from the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharma-nairātmya</s>), no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is found. Therefore the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is the general characteristic (<s>sāmānya-lakṣaṇa</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>. Such knowledge is the non-confusion regarding the general characteristic.

children.text:
viparyastamanaskārāvihāniparihāṇitaḥ /
tadaśuddhir viśuddhiś ca sa ca tatrāviparyayaḥ // V.20
children.translated_text: Due to the non-abandonment and abandonment of confused mental attention, there is its impurity and purity respectively, and the non-confusion there [is regarding that]. // V.20

body.text: viparyastasmanaskārāprahāṇan tasya dharmadhātor aviśuddhis tatprahāṇaṃ viśuddhir iti yad evaṃjñānam ayam aviśuddhau viśuddhau cāviparyāso yathākramaṃ /
body.translated_text: The non-abandonment of confused mental attention is the impurity of that <s>dharmadhātu</s>; the abandonment of it is [its] purity. Such knowledge is the non-confusion regarding impurity and purity, respectively.

children.text:
dharmadhātor viśuddhatvāt prakṛtyā vyomavat punaḥ /
dvayasyāgantukatvaṃ hi sa ca tatrāviparyayaḥ // V.21
children.translated_text: Since the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is pure by nature, like space, the adventitious nature of both [impurity and purity] — the non-confusion there [is regarding that]. // V.21

body.text: dharmadhātoḥ punar ākāśavat / prakṛtiviśuddhatvāt / dvayam apy etad āgantukam aviśuddhiru viśuddhiś ca paścād iti / yad evaṃjñānam ayam āgantukatve 'viparyāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: Since the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, like space, is pure by nature, both of these — impurity and purity — are adventitious, [impurity being present] initially [and purity] subsequently. Such knowledge is the non-confusion regarding adventitious nature.

children.text:
saṃkleśaś ca viśuddhiś ca dharmapudgalayor na hi /
asatvāt trāsatāmānau nātaḥ so 'trāviparyayaḥ // V.22
children.translated_text: For neither defilement nor purity [truly exists] with respect to <s>dharmas</s> and the person (<s>pudgala</s>), since [they are] non-existent. Therefore, fearlessness and non-elation — the non-confusion there [is regarding that]. // V.22

body.text: na hi pudgalasya saṃkleśo na viśuddhir nāpi dharmasya / yasmān na pudgalo 'sti na dharmo yataś ca na kasyacit saṃkleśo na vyavadānaṃ ato na saṃkleśapakṣe kasyacid dhāniḥ na vyavadānapakse kasyacid viśeṣaḥ / yatas trāso vā syād unnatir vety ayam atrāse 'nunnatau cāviparyāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: For there is neither defilement of the person (<s>pudgala</s>) nor purification, nor is there [defilement or purification] of <s>dharmas</s>. Since neither the person exists, nor [independently existing] <s>dharmas</s>, therefore there is defilement and purification of no one.

body.text:
[Daśa vajrapadāni]
ete ca daśāviparyāsā daśasu vajrapadeṣu yathākramaṃ yojayitavyāḥ / daśa vajrapadāni / sadasattā aviparyasaḥ / āśrayo māyopamatā avikalpanatā prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā saṃkleśo vyavadānaṃ / ākāśopamatā ahīnatā aviśiṣṭatā ca / vajrapadānāṃ śarīravyavasthānaṃ / svabhāvataḥ / ālambanataḥ / avikalpanataḥ / codyaparihārataś ca / tatra svabhāvataḥ trayaḥ svabhāvāḥ / pariniṣpannaparikalpitaparatantrākhyā ādyais tribhiḥ padair yathākramaṃ / ālambanataḥ / ta eva avikalpanato yena ca na vikalpayati nirvikalpena jñānena yac ca na vikalpayati prakṛtiprabhāsvaratāṃ / tad anena jñeyajñānavyavasthānaṃ yathākramaṃ veditavyaṃ / yad uta tribhiḥ svabhāvair avikalpanatayā ca / codyaparihārataḥ / śiṣṭāni padāni tatredaṃ codyaṃ / yady ete parikalpitaparatantralakṣaṇā dharmā na saṃvidyante / katham upalabhyante / atha saṃvidyante dharmāṇāṃ prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā na (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 69]

children.text: ) yujyate / tan māyopamatayā pariharati / yathā māyākṛtaṃ na vidyata upalabhyate ca yadi prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā dharmāṇāṃ tat kathaṃ pūrvaṃ saṃkleśaḥ paścād vyavadānaṃ / asya parihāraḥ / saṃkleśavyavadānam ākāśopamatayā veditavyaṃ / yathākāśaṃ prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ saṃkliśyate / vyavadāyate ceti / yady aprameyabuddhotpāde saty aprameyāṇāṃ satvānāṃ kleśāpaśamaḥ / tat kathaṃ na saṃsārasamucchedo na nirvāṇavṛddhir bhavati / tasyāhīnāviśiṣṭatayā parihāraḥ / aprameyatvāt satvadhātor vyavadānapakṣasya ca /
children.translated_text: This is coherent. One resolves this through the analogy with illusion (<s>māyā</s>). Just as what is produced by magic does not exist [in reality] yet is perceived — [so too,] if the natural luminosity (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā</s>) of <s>dharmas</s> is [accepted] —

body.translated_text: [The Ten Vajra-Statements (<s>daśa vajrapadāni</s>)] And these ten non-errors are to be correlated in order with the ten vajra-statements. The ten vajra-statements are: existence and non-existence, non-error —

body.text: dvitīyaṃ śarīravyavasthānam /
body.translated_text: The second is the arrangement of the body [of the text].

children.text: yatra yā ca yato bhrāntir abhrāntir yā ca yatra ca /
children.translated_text: Where and what is delusion, and from what; and what is non-delusion and where;

children.text: bhrāntyabhrāntiphale caiva paryantaś ca tayor iti //
children.translated_text: And the fruits of delusion and non-delusion, and their limit.
Non-error regarding existence and non-existence, the basis, the analogy with illusion,

children.text: akalpanā prakṛtyā ca bhāsvaratvaṃ sadaiva hi //
children.translated_text: Non-conceptualization, natural luminosity at all times,
Defilement, purification, and the analogy with space,
And being neither deficient nor excessive — these are the ten vajra-statements.

body.text: uktānudharmapratipattiḥ /
body.translated_text: The practice in accordance with what has been taught.

body.text:
[d. Antadvayavarjane pratipattiḥ]
antadvayavarjane pratipattiḥ katamā yā ratnakūṭe madhyamā pratipattir upadiṣṭā / kasyāntasya varjanād asau veditavyā /
body.translated_text: [d. Practice of avoiding the two extremes] What is the practice of avoiding the two extremes? That which is taught in the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s> as the middle practice. What is it?

children.translated_text: Separateness and oneness are extremes; and those of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhists) and <s>śrāvakas</s> as well.
The extreme of superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) and deprecation (<s>apavāda</s>) is twofold: regarding person (<s>pudgala</s>) and <s>dharmas</s>. (V.23)
The extreme of the adversary and its antidote is designated as eternalism and annihilationism.
Regarding the grasped and the grasper, defilement and purification — [the extreme is] twofold and threefold. (V.24)

children.text:
vikalpadvayatāntaś ca sa ca saptavidho mataḥ /
bhāvābhāve praśāmye 'tha śamane trāsyantadbhaye // V.25
children.translated_text: And the extreme of the duality of conceptualization — that is regarded as sevenfold: regarding existence and non-existence, regarding pacification, regarding calming, regarding what is feared and fear, (V.25)

children.text:
grāhyagrāhe 'tha samyaktvamithyātve vyāpṛtau na ca /
ajanmasamakālatve sa vikalpadvayāntatā // V.26
children.translated_text: Regarding the grasped and the grasper, regarding right and wrong, regarding engagement and non-engagement, regarding unborn-ness, sameness, and timelessness — this is the extreme of the duality of conceptualization. (V.26)
