body.text: tatra rūpādibhyaḥ / pṛthaktvam ātmana ity antaḥ / ekatvam ity antaḥ tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipat / yā nātmapratyavekṣā / yāvan na mānavapratyavekṣā ātmadarśane hi jīvas tac charīraṃ / anyo jīvo 'nyac charīram iti bhavati darśanaṃ / nityaṃ rūpam iti tīrthikāntaḥ / anityam iti śrāvakāntaḥ / tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad yā rūpādīnāṃ na nityapratyavekṣā nānityapratyavekṣā / ātmeti pudgalasamāropāntaḥ nairātmyam ity apavādāntaḥ prajñaptisato 'py apavādāt / tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad yad ātmanairātmyayor madhyaṃ nirvikalpaṃ jñānaṃ / bhūtaṃ cittam iti dharmasamāropāntaḥ abhūtam ity apavādāntaḥ / tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad yatra na cittaṃ na cetanā na mano na vijñānaṃ / akuśalādayo dharmāḥ saṃkleśa iti vipakṣāntaḥ / kuśalādayo vyavadānam iti pratipakṣāntas tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad yo 'syāntadvayasyānupagamo 'nudāhāro 'pravyāhāraḥ / astīti śāśvatāntas tayor eva pudgaladharmayor nāstīty ucchedāntas tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad yad anayor dvayor antayor madhyaṃ / avidyā grāhyā grāhakā cety antaḥ / evaṃ vidyā saṃskārā asaṃskṛtaṃ ca tatpratipakṣaḥ / yāvaj jarāmaraṇaṃ grāhyaṃ grāhakaṃ cety antas tannirodho grāhyo grāhako vety anto yena mārgeṇa tan nirudhyate / evaṃ grāhyagrāhakānto (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 71]

children.text: ) dvidhā kṛṣṇaśuklapakṣabhedena tatparivarjanārthaṃ madhyamā pratipad vidyā cāvidyā cādvayam etad iti vistareṇa vidyāvidyādīnāṃ grāhyagrāhakatvābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: It is twofold through the division into the dark and bright sides. For the purpose of avoiding those, the middle practice [is taught]: knowledge and ignorance are a non-duality — thus, in detail, because of the absence of grasped and grasper in knowledge, ignorance, and the like.

body.translated_text: Therein: the extreme that 'the self is separate from form and the like'; the extreme that 'it is one [with them]' — for the purpose of avoiding these, the middle practice [is taught]. That which is neither the assertion of self —

body.text: trividhaḥ saṃkleśaḥ / kleśasaṃkleśaḥ / karmasaṃkleśaḥ / janmasaṃkleśaś ca / tatra kleśasaṃkleśas trividhaḥ / dṛṣṭiḥ rāgadveṣamohanimittaṃ punarbhavapraṇidhānaṃ ca / yasya pratipakṣo jñānaśūnyatā jñānānimittaṃ jñānāpraṇihitaṃ ca / karmasaṃkleśaḥ / śubhāśubhakarmābhisaṃskāraḥ yasya pratipakṣo jñānānabhisaṃskāraḥ / janmasaṃkleśaḥ / punarbhavajātiḥ jātasya cittacaittānāṃ pratikṣaṇotpādaḥ / punarbhavaprabandhaś ca yasya pratipakṣo jñānājātiḥ jñānānutpādo jñānāsvabhāvatā ca / etasya trividhasya saṃkleśasyāpagamo vyavadānaṃ / tatra jñānaśūnyatādibhiḥ / jñeyaśūnyatādayo dharmā etena trividhena saṃkleśena yathāyogaṃ yāvan na śūnyatādayaḥ kriyante / prakṛtyaiva śūnyatādayo dharmadhātoḥ prakṛtyasaṃkliṣṭatvāt tena yadi dharmadhātuḥ saṃkliśyate vā viśudhyate veti kalpayaty ayam antaḥ / prakṛtyasaṃkliṣṭasya saṃkleśaviśuddhyabhāvād etasyāntasya parivarjanārthaṃ / madhyamā pratipat / yan na śūnyatayā dharmāñ chūnyāṃ karoti / api tu dharmā eva śūnyā ity evamādi /
body.translated_text: Defilement is threefold: defilement of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), defilement of <s>karma</s>, and defilement of birth (<s>janma</s>). Therein, the defilement of afflictions is threefold: views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), attachment-aversion-delusion as the cause, and the condition for further existence —

body.text: aparaḥ saptavidho vikalpadvayāntas tad yathā bhāve 'pi vikalpo 'ntaḥ/ abhāve 'pi pudgalo 'sti yasya vināśāya śūnyatā (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 72]

children.text: ) nairātmyam api vā nāstīti kalpanāt / tad etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārtham iyaṃ madhyamā pratipat / na khalu pudgalavināśāya śūnyatā api tu śūnyataiva śūnyā pūrvāntaśūnyatā / aparāntaśūnyatā ity evamādivistaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Or: 'selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) does not exist' — from such conceptualization. For the purpose of avoiding this extreme of the duality of conceptualization, this middle practice [is taught]: emptiness is certainly not for the destruction of the person, but rather —

body.translated_text: Another sevenfold extreme of the duality of conceptualization: regarding existence, conceptualization is an extreme; regarding non-existence too — 'there is a person whose destruction is [the purpose of teaching] emptiness' —

body.text: śāmye 'pi vikalpo 'ntaḥ / śamane 'pi vikalpo 'nataḥ praheyaprahāṇakalpanayā śūnyatāyās trasanād etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārtham ākāśadṛṣṭāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: Regarding pacification too, conceptualization is an extreme; regarding calming too, conceptualization is an extreme — through the conceptualization of what is to be abandoned and its abandonment. From being terrified of emptiness, for the purpose of avoiding this extreme of the duality of conceptualization, the analogy of the sky-view [is given] —

body.text: trāsye 'pi vikalpo 'ntas tataś ca trāsyād bhaye 'pi parikalpitarūpāditrasanāt (/) duḥkhabhīrutayā etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārthaṃ citrakaradṛṣṭāntaḥ / pūrvako dṛṣṭāntaḥ śrāvakān ārabhyāyaṃ tu bodhisatvān /
body.translated_text: Regarding what is feared, conceptualization is an extreme; and from that fear too — from being terrified of imagined form and the like, from fear of suffering — for the purpose of avoiding this extreme of the duality of conceptualization, the analogy of the painter [is given].

body.text: grāhye 'pi vikalpo 'ntaḥ grāhake 'pi etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārthaṃ māyākāradṛṣṭāntaḥ / vijñaptimātrajñānakṛtaṃ hy arthābhāvajñānaṃ / tac cārthābhāvajñānaṃ / tad eva vijñaptimātrajñānaṃ nivartayati / arthābhāve vijñaptyasaṃbhavād ity etad atra sādharmyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Regarding the grasped, conceptualization is an extreme; regarding the grasper too — for the purpose of avoiding this extreme of the duality of conceptualization, the analogy of the magician [is given]. For the knowledge of the absence of [external] objects arises from the knowledge of mere cognition (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>). That —

body.text: samyaktve 'pi vikalpo 'ntaḥ mithyātve 'pi bhūtapratyavekṣāṃ samyaktvena kalpayato mithyātvena vā etasyāntadvayasya parivarjanārthaṃ / kāṣṭhadvayāgnidṛṣṭāntaḥ / yathākāṣṭhadvayād (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 73]

children.text: ) anagnilakṣaṇād agnir jāyate / jātaś ca tad eva kāṣṭhadvayaṃ dahaty evam asamyaktvalakṣaṇāyā yathābhūtapratyavekṣāyāḥ samyaktvalakṣaṇam āryaṃ prajñendriyaṃ jāyate jātaṃ ca tām eva bhūtapratyavekṣāṃ vibhāvayatīty etad atra sādharmyaṃ na cāsamyaktvalakṣaṇāpi bhūtapratyavekṣā mithyātvalakṣaṇā samyaktvānukūlyāt /
children.translated_text: which do not have the characteristic of fire, fire is born, and once born, it burns those very two sticks — even so, from true examination, which does not have the characteristic of correctness, the noble faculty of wisdom (<s>prajñendriya</s>), having the characteristic of correctness, is born, and once born, it dispels that very true examination. This is the similarity here. And even though the true examination does not have the characteristic of correctness, it is not of the characteristic of incorrectness, because it is conducive to correctness.

body.translated_text: Even in correctness there is the extreme of conceptualization; even in incorrectness, [there is the extreme] of one who fabricates a true examination as being correct or as being incorrect. For the avoidance of this pair of extremes, the analogy of two sticks producing fire [is given]. Just as from two sticks,

body.text: vyāpṛtāv api vikalpo 'ntaḥ / avyāpṛtāv api jñānasya buddhipūrvāṃ kriyāṃ niḥsāmarthyaṃ vā kalpayataḥ / etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārthaṃ / tailapradyotadṛṣṭāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: Even regarding activity there is the extreme of conceptualization; even regarding non-activity — of one who fabricates either deliberate action or powerlessness of knowledge. For the avoidance of this pair of extremes of conceptualization, the analogy of a lamp [burning] oil [is given].

body.text: ajanmatve 'pi vikalpo 'ntaḥ samakālatve 'pi yadi pratipakṣasyānutpattiṃ vā kalpayati saṃkleśasyaiva vā dīrghakālatvam etasya vikalpadvayāntasya parivarjanārthaṃ dvitīyas tailapradyotadṛṣṭāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: Even regarding non-origination there is the extreme of conceptualization; even regarding simultaneity — if one fabricates either the non-arising of the antidote or the long duration of defilement alone. For the avoidance of this pair of extremes of conceptualization, the second analogy of a lamp [burning] oil [is given].

body.text: uktāntadvayaparivarjane pratipattiḥ /
body.translated_text: This is the practice of avoiding the stated pair of extremes.

body.text:
[e. Viśisṭā cāviśiṣṭā ca pratipattiḥ]
viśiṣṭā cāviśiṣṭā ca pratipattiḥ / katamā /
body.translated_text:
[e. Distinguished and undistinguished practice]
Distinguished and undistinguished practice — what is it?

body.text: viśiṣṭā cāviśiṣṭā ca jñeyā daśasu bhūmiṣu /
body.translated_text: The distinguished and the undistinguished should be known in the ten stages (<s>bhūmis</s>).

body.text: yasyāṃ bhūmau yā pāramitātiriktatarā sā tatra viśiṣṭā sarvāsu ca sarvatra samudāgacchatīty aviśiṣṭā /
body.translated_text: In whichever stage a particular <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) is preeminent, that is distinguished there; and since all [perfections] are accomplished everywhere [in all stages], it is undistinguished.

body.text: uktaṃ pratipattyānuttaryaṃ /
body.translated_text: The unsurpassedness of practice has been stated.

body.text:
[3. Ālambanānuttarya]
ālambanānuttaryaṃ / katamat /
body.translated_text:
[3. Unsurpassedness of the object-support (<s>ālambanānuttarya</s>)]
The unsurpassedness of the object-support — what is it?

children.translated_text: Establishment, and the <s>dhātu</s> (element), what is to be accomplished and the means of accomplishment, retention — // V.27
Ascertainment and discernment, penetration, extension,

children.text: pragamaḥ praśaṭhatvaṃ ca prakarṣālambanaṃ mataṃ // V.28
children.translated_text: Progression, openness — these are regarded as the supreme object-supports. // V.28

body.text: ity etat / dvādaśavidham ālambanaṃ / yad uta dharmaprajñaptivyavasthānālambanaṃ dharmadhātvālambanaṃ sādhyālambanaṃ sādhanālambanaṃ / dhāraṇālambanaṃ avadhāraṇālambanaṃ / pradhāraṇālambanaṃ / prativedhālambanaṃ / pratānatālambanaṃ / pragamālambanaṃ / praśaṭhatvālambanaṃ prakarṣālambanaṃ ca / tatra prathamaṃ ye pāramitādayo dharmā vyavasthāpyante / dvitīyan tathatā tṛtīyacaturthe te eva yathākramaṃ dharmadhātuprativedhena pāramitādidharmādhigamāt / pañcamaṃ śrutamayajñānālambanaṃ / ṣaṣṭhaṃ / cintāmayasyāvagamya dhāraṇāt / saptamaṃ bhāvanāmayasya pratyātmaṃ dhāraṇāt / aṣṭamaṃ prathamāyāṃ bhūmau darśanamārgasya / navamaṃ bhāvanāmārgasya yāvat saptamyāṃ bhūmau / daśamaṃ tatraiva laukikalokottarasya mārgasya / prakāraśo dharmādhigamāt / ekādaśam aṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau dvādaśaṃ navamyādibhūmitraye tad eva hi prathamadvayaṃ / tasyān tasyām avasthāyāṃ tattadālambanaṃ nāma labhate /
body.translated_text: Thus, the object-support is twelvefold, namely: (1) the object-support of the establishment of <s>dharma</s>-designations; (2) the object-support of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>; (3) the object-support of what is to be accomplished; (4) the object-support of the means of accomplishment; (5) the object-support of retention; (6) the object-support of ascertainment; (7) the object-support of discernment; (8) the object-support of penetration; (9) the object-support of extension; (10) the object-support of progression; (11) the object-support of openness; and (12) the object-support of supremacy. Therein, the first is [the object-support] where <s>dharmas</s> such as the <s>pāramitās</s> are established. The second is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). The third and fourth are those same [dharmas and tathatā] respectively, because of the attainment of <s>dharmas</s> such as the <s>pāramitās</s> through the penetration of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. The fifth is the object-support of knowledge born of learning (<s>śrutamayajñāna</s>). The sixth is [the object-support] of knowledge born of reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>), through retaining what has been understood. The seventh is [the object-support] of knowledge born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>), through retaining [it] within one's own [experience]. The eighth is [the object-support] of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) on the first stage. The ninth is [the object-support] of the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) up to the seventh stage. The tenth is [the object-support] of the mundane and supramundane path on that same [seventh stage], through the attainment of <s>dharmas</s> in various ways. The eleventh is on the eighth stage. The twelfth is in the three stages beginning with the ninth — for it is indeed the first pair [of accomplishment and means]. In each successive stage, [the object-support] receives its respective designation.

body.text: uktam ālambanaṃ //
body.translated_text: The object-support has been stated.

body.text:
[4. Samudāgamānuttarya]
samudāgamaḥ katamaḥ /
body.translated_text:
[4. Unsurpassedness of accomplishment (<s>samudāgamānuttarya</s>)]
What is the accomplishment?

children.text:
avaikalyāpratikṣepo 'vikṣepaś ca prapūraṇā /
samutpādo nirūḍhiś ca karmaṇyatvāpratiṣṭhitā /
nirāvaraṇatā tasyāprasrabdhisamudāgamaḥ // V.29

body.text: ity eṣa daśavidhaḥ samudāgamaḥ / tatra pratyayāvaikalyaṃ / gotrasamudāgamaḥ / (

children.translated_text: [Mvbh 75]

children.text: ) mahāyānāpratikṣepo 'dhimuktisamudāgamaḥ / hīnayānāvikṣepaś cittotpādasamudāgamaḥ / pāramitāparipūraṇā pratipattisamudāgamaḥ / āryamārgotpādo niyāmāvakrāntisamudāgamaḥ / kuśalamūlanirūḍhiḥ dīrghakālaparicayāt satvaparipākasamudāgamaḥ [/] cittakarmaṇyatvaṃ kṣetrapariśuddhisamudāgamaḥ / saṃsāranirvāṇāpratiṣṭhatā avinivartanīyabhūmivyākaraṇalābhasamudāgamaḥ saṃsāranirvāṇābhyām avinivartanāt / nirāvaraṇatā buddhabhūmisamudāgamaḥ / tadaprasrabdhir bodhisaṃdarśanasamudāgamaḥ [//]
children.translated_text: Non-rejection of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is the accomplishment of aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>). Non-distraction toward the lesser vehicle is the accomplishment of the arising of the mind [of awakening] (<s>cittotpāda</s>). Fulfillment of the <s>pāramitās</s> is the accomplishment of practice (<s>pratipatti</s>). The arising of the noble path is the accomplishment of entry into the certainty [of awakening] (<s>niyāmāvakrānti</s>). The growth of wholesome roots through long habituation is the accomplishment of the maturation of beings (<s>sattvaparipāka</s>). Workability of mind is the accomplishment of the purification of the [Buddha-]field (<s>kṣetrapariśuddhi</s>). Non-abiding in either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s> is the accomplishment of obtaining the prediction at the irreversible stage (<s>avinivartanīyabhūmivyākaraṇalābha</s>), because one does not turn back from either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Freedom from obstruction is the accomplishment of the <s>Buddha</s>-stage (<s>buddhabhūmi</s>). Non-relaxation of that is the accomplishment of the display of awakening (<s>bodhisaṃdarśana</s>).

body.translated_text: This accomplishment is tenfold. Therein, non-deficiency of conditions is the accomplishment of the spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>).

body.text:
[Śāstranāmavyākhyāna]
ity etac
body.translated_text:
[Explanation of the title of the treatise]
This —

children.translated_text: This treatise is the <s>Madhyavibhāga</s> (Distinguishing the Middle),

body.text: madhyamāpratipatprakāśanāt madhyāntavibhāgam apy etan madhyasyāntayoś ca prakāśanāt / ādyaparavarjitasya madhyasya vā /
body.translated_text: because it illuminates the middle path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>). It is also the <s>Madhyāntavibhāga</s> (Distinguishing the Middle and the Extremes), because it illuminates the middle and the extremes — that is, the middle which is free from both the first and the last [extremes].

body.text: gūḍhasārārtham eva ca /
body.translated_text: And it has a hidden essential meaning,

body.text: tarkasyāgocaratvāt paravādibhir abhedyatvāc ca yathākramaṃ /
body.translated_text: because it is beyond the reach of [mere] reasoning, and because it cannot be refuted by opponents — respectively.

body.text: mahārthaṃ caiva /
body.translated_text: And it has a great purpose,

body.text: svaparādhikārāt /
body.translated_text: because it benefits both oneself and others.

body.text: sarvārthaṃ /
body.translated_text: And it concerns all purposes,

body.text: yānatrayādhikārāt /
body.translated_text: because it treats of the three vehicles.

children.translated_text: It dispels all harm. // V.30

body.text: kleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇāvāhanāt /
body.translated_text: Because it conveys the abandonment of the obstructions of affliction (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and the obstructions to the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>).

body.text:
[Yānānuttaryapiṇḍārtha]
ānuttaryasya piṇḍārthaḥ / samāsatas trividham ānuttaryaṃ pratipattiḥ (/) pratipattyādhāraḥ pratipattiphalaṃ caiva / sā ca pratipattir yādṛśī paramā / yena ca
body.translated_text:
[Summary meaning of the unsurpassedness of the vehicle (<s>yānānuttaryapiṇḍārtha</s>)]
The summary meaning of unsurpassedness: In brief, unsurpassedness is threefold — practice, the basis of practice, and the fruit of practice. And that practice [is understood in terms of] what sort of supreme [practice it is], and by what

body.text: yathāprajñaptito dharmamahāyānamanaskriyā (V. 7ab)
body.translated_text: according to the designation of <s>dharma</s> and <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the mental engagement (V. 7ab)

body.text: ity evamādinā / yathā yena prakāreṇāvikṣepapariṇatā ca śamathabhāvanayā aviparyāsapariṇatā ca vipaśyanābhāvanayā/ yadarthaṃ ca madhyamayā pratipadā niryāṇārthaṃ / yatra ca
body.translated_text: and so forth in this manner — by what mode it is transformed through non-distraction, through the cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), and transformed through non-inversion, through the cultivation of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). And for what purpose — for the purpose of deliverance through the middle path. And where —

body.text: daśasu bhūmiṣu (V. 27b) /
body.translated_text: in the ten stages (V. 27b).

body.text: viśiṣṭā cāviśiṣṭā ca (V. 27a) /
body.translated_text: Distinguished and undistinguished (V. 27a).

body.text: aviparyāsānāṃ piṇḍārthaḥ / vyañjanāviparyāsena śamathanimittaṃ pratividhyati / arthāviparyāsena vipaśyanānimittaṃ pratividhyati / manaskārāviparyāsena viparyāsanidānaṃ parivarjayati / avisārāviparyāsena tannimittaṃ sugṛhītaṃ karoti / svalakṣaṇāviparyāsena tatpratipakṣeṇāvikalpaṃ mārgaṃ bhāvayati / sāmānyalakṣaṇāviparyāsena vyavadānaprakṛtiṃ pratividhyati / aśuddhiśuddhimanaskārāviparyāsena tadāvaraṇaprahīṇāprahīṇatāṃ prajānāti / tadāgantukatvāviparyāsena saṃkleśavyavadānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / atrāsānunnatyaviparyāsena nirāvaraṇe niryāti /
body.translated_text: The summary meaning of non-inversions: Through non-inversion of the letter, one penetrates the sign of <s>śamatha</s>. Through non-inversion of meaning, one penetrates the sign of <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Through non-inversion of mental engagement, one avoids the cause of inversion. Through non-inversion of non-deviation, one makes that sign well-grasped. Through non-inversion of specific characteristics, one cultivates the non-conceptual path as its antidote. Through non-inversion of general characteristics, one penetrates the nature of purification. Through non-inversion of the mental engagement of impure and pure, one discerns the abandoned and unabandonedness of its obstructions. Through non-inversion of their adventitious nature, one knows defilement and purification as they truly are. Through non-inversion of non-depression and non-elation therein, one proceeds to the unobstructed [state].

body.text: ānuttaryaparicchedaḥ pañcamaḥ //
body.translated_text: The fifth chapter, the Delimitation of Unsurpassedness (<s>Ānuttaryapariccheda</s>).

body.text: // samāpto madhyāntavibhāgaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus is completed the <s>Madhyāntavibhāga</s>.

body.text: // vyākhyām imām upanibadhya yad asti puṇyaṃ

children.translated_text: may that be for the arising of merit of the great world.
And for the arising of knowledge, whence comes great prosperity,

children.text: bodhitrayaṃ ca na cirāj jagad aśnuvīta //
children.translated_text: may the world soon attain the threefold awakening (<s>bodhi</s>).

body.translated_text: Whatever merit there is from composing this commentary —

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: madhyāntavibhāgakārikābhāṣyaṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Madhyāntavibhāgakārikābhāṣya</s> (Commentary on the Verses Distinguishing the Middle from the Extremes) is completed.

body.text: // kṛtir ācāryabhadantavasubandhoḥ /
body.translated_text: The composition of the master, the venerable <s>Vasubandhu</s>.
